15: Obviousness of claims 1 and 7-15 over Littlechild in view of Finkenzeller; Board's rejection affirmed
We therefore conclude that Littlechild in view of Finkenzeller renders the claims obvious.
16: Obviousness of claims 25-26 and 28-29 over Littlechild in view of Stewart; Board's rejection affirmed
We thus conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's findings and that it correctly affirmed the examiner's obviousness rejections under this ground as well.
17: Obviousness of claim 27 over Eglise in view of Finkenzeller; Board's rejection affirmed
Thus, we conclude that the Board correctly affirmed the examiner's obviousness rejections under this final ground as well.
24: Obviousness of claims 1 and 2 of the '483 patent over Tomonori in view of Sadaie; Board's finding of obviousness affirmed under substantial evidence review.
we conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that claims 1 and 2 of the '483 patent would have been obvious.
25: Obviousness of claim 3 of the '483 patent (curved back wall) over Tomonori in view of Sadaie; Board's nonobviousness finding reversed.
For these reasons, we conclude that the Board erred when it found that the combination of Tomonori and Sadaie did not render claim 3 obvious.
30: Obviousness of claim 13: the court affirmed the Board's finding under substantial evidence that the Tatsuzuki spring meets the 'axially lengthwise contact' limitation (contact beyond a point).
We disagree, and find that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the Tatsuzuki spring contacts the post at more than just a point.
67: Obviousness of Apple's '721 patent claim 8 over Neonode and Plaisant; the court held the claim obvious as a matter of law.
We reverse the judgment of infringement and no invalidity because the asserted claim of the '721 patent would have been obvious in light of Neonode and Plaisant.
68: Obviousness of Apple's '172 patent claim 18 over Robinson and Xrgomics; the court held the claim obvious as a matter of law.
Claim 18 of the '172 patent would have been obvious to one of skill in the art as a matter of law.
78: Obviousness of claims 1, 7, 12, 13 and 57 of the '550 patent over Betts and Tucker.
we affirm the Commission's determination that claims 1, 7, 12, 13, and 57 of the '550 patent are obvious.
86: Obviousness of claims 1-17 of the '268 patent over the combined prior art, including whether Monroe discloses a resilient cable or member, supported by substantial evidence.
Notwithstanding the arguments concerning waiver, we find that the Board's conclusion that Monroe discloses a "resilient" retainer is supported by substantial evidence.
87: Motivation to combine the prior art references; the Board's path was reasonably discernable and the combinations were simple substitution, so obviousness was properly found.

Taken together, we may reasonably discern that the Board found a motivation to combine the references because doing so would have been a matter of simple substitution that would result in an eyeglass retainer with certain advantages.
99: Obviousness of claims 1 and 43 of the '475 and '280 patents over Baveja and Shell; the Board found no reason to combine with a reasonable expectation of success, and the Federal Circuit affirmed that nonobviousness finding.

We agree with Depomed that the Board applied the correct legal standard in its obviousness analysis and that substantial evidence supports its finding that Purdue failed to establish that a person of ordinary skill in the art would have had a reason to combine Baveja and Shell to pursue the claimed invention with a reasonable expectation of success.
105: Summary judgment of invalidity for obviousness of claims 1, 2, 5-12, 17, 34, and 35 of U.S. Patent No. 7,991,380; affirmed.
granting summary judgment of invalidity of claims 1, 2, 5–12, 17, 34, and 35 of U.S. Patent No. 7,991,380 for anticipation and obviousness
113: Obviousness of claim 1 of the '967 patent over Fields and Su; Board's obviousness finding reversed for lack of substantial evidence, so claim 1 (and dependent claims 4, 8, 9, 12, 16, 19-22) held nonobvious.
We reverse the Board's conclusion that claim 1 of the '967 patent would have been obvious in light of Fields and Su.
121: Obviousness of the asserted Halo patent claims: the court affirmed that the claims were not invalid for obviousness.
We therefore affirm the judgment that the asserted claims of the Halo patents were not invalid for obviousness.
124: Obviousness of claims 26, 28, and 30-33 of the '084 patent over Porras in combination with Cheswick in IBM's proceeding, IPR2014-00682.
We therefore affirm the Board's determination in IBM's proceeding, IPR201400682, that claims 26, 28, and 30–33 would have been obvious.
194: Obviousness of claims 45 and 107 of the '447 patent over JP '700, JP '889 and Wang (CMOS camera substitution, secondary considerations)
We therefore hold that the Board correctly concluded that it would have been obvious to use a CMOS camera in the vehicular vision systems of JP '700 and JP '889.
195: Obviousness of claims 3 and 5-9 of the '331 patent over JP '700 and JP '889 (horizontal graphic overlay, secondary considerations)
We therefore hold that the Board correctly concluded that it would have been obvious to use the graphic overlay of JP '889 with the vehicular vision system of JP '700.
204: Obviousness of claim 1 and related claims of the '532 patent over Bambot and Weigl; Board's combination holding affirmed, teaching away rejected.
Consequently, the Board did not err in concluding that combining Bambot with Weigl rendered the claims obvious, regardless of Weigl's extra-vessel sensors.
209: Obviousness of claims 1 and 2 of the '431 patent over Li, Yamaura, Zhaung and Beta, including the pairwise motivation-to-combine approach and the motivation to combine Li and Yamaura; Board found claims unpatentable and the court affirmed.
Thus, on the facts of this case, we find no error in the Board’s approach.
210: Whether the combination of Li, Yamaura, Zhaung and Beta disclosed a core band substantially centered at the operating center frequency; court held the Board's finding supported by substantial evidence.
We also agree with Ericsson that the Board’s finding that the combination would have taught or suggested a centered core band is supported by substantial evidence.
216: Obviousness of asserted claims 1, 3, 4, 6, 26, 32-37, 39 and 42 of the '532 patent over Machinery Update articles combined with prior-art cookie packages; summary judgment of invalidity affirmed, including rejection of objective indicia.
For the reasons we have set forth, we agree with the district court that the same conclusion is warranted in this case.
228: Obviousness of claims 1-32 over Chiba and Aulton, including motivation to combine; Board found obvious and court affirmed
We, therefore, find no legal error in the Board's treatment of the motivation to combine evidence nor do we find a lack of substantial evidence supporting its conclusion.
229: Objective indicia of nonobviousness: unexpected results argument waived for dependent claims; nexus for commercial success, industry praise and long-felt need rejected

Because we agree with the Board that Novartis failed to establish a nexus between the claims and all purported evidence of nonobviousness—including commercial success—we need not and do not reach the Board's additional grounds for rejecting this evidence.
234: Unpatentability of all reexamined claims (1-42, claims 2-42 rejected after claim 1 cancelled) as obvious over the asserted prior art, affirmed as a consequence of the claim construction.
We therefore affirm the Board’s decision that all claims of the ’772 patent are unpatentable.
241: Obviousness of claim 1 over Cooper, Saggio and Lee: no clear or obvious error in finding insufficient motivation to combine.
we cannot say that the district court committed a clear or obvious error when it found insufficient motivation to combine these disparate references.
254: Obviousness of claims 5-17 and 25 based on the 'informing the mobile station' limitation, the different-generations limitation (GSM), and the forced handover request message, handover query and rejection message limitations (PACS); court affirmed the Board's obviousness findings.
We affirm the Board's finding of obviousness with respect to claims 5–17 and 25.
255: Motivation to combine McDonald, Anderson, GSM and PACS to arrive at the challenged claims (other than the vacated reactivation limitation); court affirmed the Board's finding of motivation to combine.

We also affirm the Board's finding of a motivation to combine McDonald, Anderson, GSM, and PACS to arrive at the combinations recited in the challenged claims except for the "arrangement for reactivating the link" limitation.
306: Obviousness of the '050 purity patent over the prior-art ISB mixture: the court found no substantial question of obviousness given the patentable weight of the purification process and secondary considerations.
We see no error in the district court’s analysis.
310: Obviousness of claims 1-5, 7-11, 13, and 14 of the '648 patent over Arakane; the Board's finding that Arakane teaches combining HT and ET compounds to form a light emitting layer regardless of energy gap was upheld
Thus, the Board reasonably concluded that Arakane teaches that a light-producing device can be made
332: Obviousness of claims 1-29 over Weinstein, RFC 1190, Gurrie and ISI, including motivation to combine; Board's unpatentability finding affirmed.
We have considered AIP's remaining arguments, including its obviousness arguments, and find them unpersuasive.
361: Obviousness of the 'hinged to' claims 8, 9 and 16-23 over Matsumiya in view of Deng: held unpatentable as obvious, affirming the Board
we conclude that claims 8, 9, and 16–23 at issue on appeal are unpatentable as obvious over Matsumiya in view of Deng.
362: Obviousness of the 'protuberance on' claims 11, 12 and 14: Board had found them obvious; court held them not unpatentable under the corrected construction
We therefore conclude that claims 11, 12, and 14 are not unpatentable as obvious.
363: Obviousness of the 'protuberance formed on' claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 24 on cross-appeal: held not unpatentable as obvious, affirming the Board
we find no error in the Board's analysis and its underlying factual findings and conclude that claims 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, and 24 at issue on cross-appeal are not unpatentable as obvious.
386: Obviousness of claims 12, 15, 16 over Saxton combined with Pfister: reversed because no disclosure of a first short spine was shown.
Because we hold that such components cannot be considered 'spines' under the '311 patent, there has been no showing of a disclosure or teaching of a 'first short spine' in the prior art of record.
404: Obviousness of challenged ’556 Patent claims over Ginter; Board's obviousness rejection affirmed.
Dr. Arunachalam has failed to show the Board committed a reversible error in its decision to affirm the Examiner’s anticipation and obviousness rejections over Ginter.
502: Obviousness of claims 2, 3, 5 and 6 over Smith and Wingate; affirmed on the same threshold value finding.
Because the Board did not err in its unpatentability findings or conclusions, we affirm.
503: Obviousness of claims 1-2 of the '829 patent over the prior art 50/50 mixture and pure (6S) isomer; motivation to purify and rebuttal by secondary considerations
we agree with the district court that the claimed substantially pure compound would have been obvious over both the 50/50 mixture and the pure (6S) isomer compound in the prior art.
519: Obviousness of claims 1, 5, 7, 9, 11, 16-19, 23, 32, 39-41, 63, 70-72 of the '840 patent and claims 32 and 44 of the '550 patent over Tucker and Betts; Commission's nonobviousness finding reversed for lack of substantial evidence.

Because the Commission's factual findings regarding nonobviousness are not supported by substantial evidence, we reverse on the issue of obviousness and hold that claims 1, 5, 7, 9, 11, 16–19, 23, 32, 39–41, 63, and 70–72 of the ’840 patent and claims 32 and 44 of the ’550 patent are rendered obvious by the combination of Tucker and Betts.
538: Obviousness of the chelating-agent-free acetylcysteine formulation over the EDTA-containing Acetadote label, FDA approval and Chemistry Review, and the Guilford reference. The court found no reasonable expectation of success, a finding not clearly erroneous, so the claims were nonobvious.
That finding is not clearly erroneous.
585: Obviousness of claims 1-6 of the '205 patent over Brohoff in view of Galitz, including analogous art and motivation to combine, affirmed by the court.
We affirm the Board's determination that claims 1–6 of the '205 patent were obvious in No. 2015–1810.
597: Obviousness of claims of the '413 patent over Lehr, Cockrell and Kristiansen; Board erred by shifting the burden of persuasion to the patentee and lacked substantial evidence of a motivation to combine, so the obviousness holding was reversed.
Where, as here, it is clear that the Board did not require the petitioner to support its claim of obviousness by a preponderance of the evidence, we must reverse.
598: Obviousness of claims 1, 6, 22, 30, 33, 36, 39-41, and 48 of the '859 patent; reason to combine and reasonable expectation of success, objective indicia rejected at summary judgment; claims held obvious
We agree with MacDermid that the asserted claims of the '859 patent would have been obvious at the time of the invention over the cited prior art.
604: Obviousness of claim 20 of the '944 patent (transdermal application of testosterone to the axilla); district court found claim obvious and Federal Circuit affirmed.

We agree with the district court that the prior art (e.g. the Aschkenasy '268 publication and the Cutter 2000 and 2001 references) teach and suggest that applying testosterone to the axilla will increase a patient's testosterone level with a reasonable expectation of success.
605: Invalidity of claims 9 and 10 of the '861 patent over Gueret references; district court found not invalid and Federal Circuit affirmed.
we detect no reversible error in the district court's conclusion that Amneal failed to meet its burden of proving the asserted '861 patent claims invalid.
620: Obviousness of claim 1 and claims 2-3, 5-8, 12-22, 24-33 over Cook and Saarinen. Majority held no substantial evidence supports the Board's findings that Cook teaches the icon/corresponding list and first list limitations, so the claims are nonobvious.
Because claim 1 would not have been obvious, we reverse as to claims 2–3, 5–8, 12–22, and 24–33 as well.
621: Obviousness of claim 9 over Cook (configuration icon limitation). Majority held the claim nonobvious; the dissent also would reverse on claim 9, so no judge dissented on this issue.
I would reverse the Board's decision that claim 9 would have been obvious over Cook.
622: Obviousness of dependent claims 4 and 23, which the majority held nonobvious because they depend from nonobvious claims 2 and 3; majority did not reach Lemay's separate arguments.
Therefore, claims 4, 9, and 23 also are nonobvious.
638: Obviousness of claims 1, 2, 11-15 and 25 of the '657 patent over van der Zee, Bluetooth Specification and Science Friday transcript; Board affirmed rejection as obvious.
we conclude that claims 1, 2, 11–15, and 25 of the ’657 patent would have been obvious in view of the cited references and therefore affirm the decision of the Board.
643: Obviousness of the '250 patent over Hitachi combined with Sanyo or Glenn; court found no motivation to combine and the patent nonobvious

Because the weight of the evidence supports the court’s finding that there was no motivation to combine these references, we affirm the court’s conclusion that Everlight failed to prove that the ’250 patent would have been obvious.
645: Obviousness of the '870 patent over Waitl combined with Nitta; no motivation to combine and the patent nonobvious
We thus affirm the district court’s conclusion that Everlight failed to prove the ’870 patent invalid as obvious.
647: Obviousness of the '589 patent over Nakashima combined with Kim; no motivation to combine and the patent nonobvious

We thus affirm the district court’s conclusion that one of ordinary skill in the art would not have been motivated to combine these two references and thus the references did not render the ’589 patent obvious.
656: Obviousness of claims 1 and 2 over Varga; the court held the claims obvious and affirmed the rejection.

Under this claim interpretation, Gorelik does not contest that the Board's finding that Varga renders claims 1 and 2 obvious is supported by substantial evidence. We thus affirm the Patent Office's rejection of claims 1 and 2 as obvious over Varga.
657: Obviousness of claims 3 and 4 over Varga in view of Jiang; the court held the claims obvious and affirmed, rejecting the impracticality argument as unsupported by evidence.
Gorelik fails to submit any evidence beyond conjecture to support its contention that the combination of the references would result in a very large device.
658: Obviousness of claims 1-22 and 24-26 of the '630 patent over the '375 patent and Laird; Board's finding affirmed
We agree with PacBio that the Board did not err in its obviousness determination as to claims 1–22 and 24–26
666: Obviousness of '385 patent claims 1, 5, 6 over Ohashi/Hasegawa in view of Yamamoto; motivation to combine upheld on substantial evidence
We conclude that the Board did not err in determining that claims 1, 5, and 6 of the '385 patent would have been obvious over Ohashi or Hasegawa in view of Yamamoto.
667: Obviousness of '385 patent claims 5 and 6 over He and Yamamoto
We affirm the Board's conclusion that claims 5 and 6 would have been obvious over He and Yamamoto
670: Obviousness of '765 patent claims 1, 2, 14, 16 over Ohashi and Hasegawa; motivation to combine upheld
We agree with the Alliance that substantial evidence supports the Board's findings for claims 1, 2, 14, and 16.
672: Obviousness of '765 patent claims 3 and 4 over Ohashi and Hasegawa, vacated for reconsideration under corrected claim construction
we vacate its obviousness determination as to claim 4 and remand for further consideration under the proper construction.
673: Obviousness of '765 patent claims 11 and 12 over Ohashi, Hasegawa and Yamamoto; combinability arguments rejected
Thus, we affirm the Board's obviousness determinations as to claims 11 and 12 for the same reasons we stated above.
676: Obviousness of claims 1-14 of the '070 patent over the prior art
The Board did not err in concluding the asserted claims would have been obvious.
694: Obviousness of independent claims 1, 14 and dependents (claims 1-3, 6, 7, 14, 17-19) over Alumot in view of Moriya; Board affirmed, court affirmed
We affirm the Board's decision that claims 1–3, 6, 7, 14, and 17–19 are obvious over the prior art
695: Obviousness of claim 9 and dependents (claims 9-11) requiring training a model using multiple known good substrates; court reversed, finding no substantial evidence
Accordingly, we find claim 9 not obvious over Alumot in view of Moriya.
718: Obviousness of challenged claims 1, 2, 5, 8, 10, 11, 14, 17-19, 22, 25-27, 30, 33 of the '805 patent over CustomerSat, Medinets and HTML Spec, including the Board's treatment of background knowledge of a skilled artisan and expert credibility; Board found claims not unpatentable.
We agree with OpinionLab that the Board did not err in reaching its conclusion that the challenged claims are not unpatentable as obvious.
747: Obviousness of claims 15-17, 33 and 35 over Bevins and Morita, affirmed on the basis of the Board's claim construction
Having found that the Board correctly construed the claims of the ’587 patent, we affirm the anticipation and obviousness determinations.
772: Obviousness of interposing claims 6, 7, 13, 15-18 and 21 over Munnekehoff or Barmag in view of Ligon; Board's tube Q finding was ambiguous and fact findings were left to the Board, so the obviousness ruling was vacated and remanded.
773: Obviousness of claim 4 over Munnekehoff or Barmag in view of Bluhm; Board found claim 4 obvious and the court affirmed.
The Board's factual findings are supported by substantial evidence and we see no error in its conclusion of obviousness.
792: Obviousness of claim 7 of the '343 patent; the court reversed cancellation because the relied-on prior art (Goertzen) lacks the claimed perpendicular mounting plate element.
Accordingly, there is no evidence of the claim 7 element in the relied-on prior art.
793: Obviousness of the remaining claims of the '598 and '343 patents over Goertzen combined with Hosino (and Schaffner or Mulhern), including motivation to lower the pivot and the reasonable expectation of compensating for instability; the court affirmed cancellation.
806: Obviousness under pre-AIA §103 of all claims of the ’272 Patent over Birrell and Cunniff. The Board's conclusion lacked substantial-evidence support on the motivation to combine, the expectation of success, and the claimed multiple lockable buffers, so the court vacated.
Because the Board’s obviousness conclusion is based on findings not supported by substantial evidence, we vacate the Board’s decision.
815: Obviousness of claims 1-7 and 18 of the '599 patent over Figa and Martensson, including the processor means elements and motivation to combine. Board found the claims obvious; affirmed under substantial evidence review.
we conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's obviousness determinations.
819: Obviousness of claims 7 and 10 over Laverick and Mack. The court affirmed the Board's finding that the claims would not have been obvious.
We therefore affirm the Board's decision that claims 7 and 10 would not have been obvious.
820: Obviousness of method claims 16 and 17 over Mack alone. The court reversed the Board's finding of obviousness because the Board failed to explain a motivation to fixedly secure Mack's motor and the finding that Mack suggests the limitation lacked substantial evidence.
We therefore reverse the Board's decision that claims 16 and 17 would have been obvious.
857: Obviousness of reexamined claims 118 et al. of the '175 patent over Pinnow, Stevenson and Nakamura, including motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success
We therefore uphold the Board's decision rejecting the disputed claims of the '175 patent.
858: Objective indicia of nonobviousness (secondary considerations: industry praise, licensing, commercial success) found insufficient to outweigh prima facie obviousness
we sustain the Board's conclusion that the evidence of commercial success did not outweigh the strong prima facie showing of obviousness.
860: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) of claims 1-9 and 11-13 of Application No. 13/559,194 over Swartz, Medamana, Hammad and Skowronek; Board affirmed the examiner's rejections and the court affirmed.
Accordingly, he has failed to show that the Board's decision was unsupported by substantial evidence.
884: Obviousness of the independent claims (all three patents) over the CRD-5500 Manual, affirmed as obvious.

Because the Board's obviousness-related findings with respect to the CRD-5500 Manual are supported by substantial evidence, and because those findings are sufficient to support its ultimate legal conclusion of obviousness, we affirm the Board's finding that the independent claims are obvious.
885: Obviousness of dependent claims 14, 15 and 24 ('unique identifier', 'world wide name', 'host device ID' limitations), affirmed as obvious over the CRD-5500 Manual combined with HP Journal and Fibre Channel standard.
We disagree. For "unique identifier," the Board found that the channel numbers in the CRD-5500 manual uniquely identify the host.
927: Obviousness of dependent claims 4, 7, and 15 over Schober in combination with Eckart patents
we affirm the district court's summary judgment of invalidity of claims 4, 7, and 15 as being obvious in view of Schober in combination with the Eckart patents.
928: Obviousness of design patent D'068 over Exhibit 5 combined with Schober
we conclude that the district court did not err in holding that the D'068 patent is invalid as obvious in light of Exhibit 5 combined with Schober.
933: Obviousness of claims 7-12 over Lue in view of Lawton; Board's finding of no reasonable expectation of success lacked substantial evidence, so claims held obvious.
we reverse the Board's conclusion that claims 7–12 would not have been obvious.
941: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) of claims 16, 25, and 34 of application 11/497,047 over Murphy and Mizuno, including whether Mizuno is analogous art and whether the combination was proper.
We agree with the PTO that the Board did not err in concluding that the cited prior art references rendered the claims obvious.
943: Obviousness of claims 1-31 of the '567 application over Pallas, including whether the PTO established a prima facie case, reasonable expectation of success for the cloud point limitation, and burden allocation. The Board's obviousness holding was vacated for failure to articulate reasoning and for improperly shifting the burden to the applicant.

Because the Board failed to adequately articulate its reasoning, erroneously rejected relevant evidence of nonobviousness, and improperly shifted to Stepan the burden of proving patentability, we vacate the Board's decision that claims 1–31 of the '567 application would have been obvious.
948: Obviousness of claim 21 over Henriksson and Sasaki: no substantial question of validity, so the claim was held nonobvious for preliminary injunction purposes.
we conclude that the district court did not abuse its discretion in rejecting Toro's obviousness defense and determining that Toro did not raise a substantial question of validity.
956: Obviousness of claims 1-15 of the '384 patent over Fukuta in view of Morris; Board found principle of operation would be fundamentally altered, so claims not obvious.

We agree with Sulzer that the Board's definition of Fukuta's "principle of operation" and the Board's finding that combining Fukuta and Morris would fundamentally alter that "principle of operation" are supported by substantial evidence.
957: Obviousness of claims 1-15 over Jacobsen in view of Hunter; combination would render Jacobsen inoperable for its intended purpose, so claims not obvious.
Accordingly, the Board did not err in concluding that claims 1–15 would not have been obvious over Jacobsen in view of Hunter.
962: Obviousness of claims 7, 11, 19 and 21 over Kobayashi and Kikuchi; Board finding of obviousness affirmed

We affirm the Board's conclusions that it would have been obvious to combine Kobayashi and Kikuchi, and that the challenged claims of the '549 patent would have been obvious over a combination of the prior art references.
969: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103 of asserted claims 5, 6, 10, 13 and 14 of the '770 patent over the '800 patent and other prior art, including the treatment of the claimed patient subset and rejection of secondary considerations.
We affirm the district court's holding that the challenged claims of the '770 patent would have been obvious over the '800 patent and other prior art.
982: Obviousness of claims 21-34 and 36-37 over Sibbet in view of '088 Stoller and other references: the court affirmed the Board's finding that the three-layer laminated claims would have been obvious, and rejected the applicant's teaching-away and motivation arguments.
Because the Board's findings underlying its obviousness rejections are supported by substantial evidence, we affirm the rejections of claims 21-34 and 36-37.
987: Obviousness of reexamined claims 1-42 of the '301 patent over the Summers, Dow and UL-719 combination; the Board erred in relying on inherency but the error was harmless, and the obviousness rejection was affirmed.
However, we also conclude that the Board’s error was harmless because, although it improperly invoked inherency, it need not have.
988: Objective indicia (long-felt need and nexus) of nonobviousness: the Board properly found Southwire's evidence lacked factual support and nexus, and that any long-felt need was already met by Summers.

We agree with Cerro. Substantial evidence supports the Board’s findings that Southwire’s evidence lacked factual support, that its objective evidence lacked a nexus to the claimed invention, and that any long-felt need adduced from the evidence had already been met by Summers.
1054: Obviousness of claims 62-64, 67-69, 71-73, 75, and 77-85 of the '662 application over Astiz in view of Zimmerman, including whether the references could be combined.

We agree with the Director that substantial evidence supports the Board's determination that one of ordinary skill in the art would have combined Astiz and Zimmerman to render the claimed subject matter obvious.
1057: Obviousness of claims 1-13 of application 12/023,047 over Doi in view of Weinle (and Conner for claim 6); Board found Doi does not teach away and substantial evidence supports motivation to combine.
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's obviousness determination, we affirm the final rejection of claims 1–13 of the '047 application.
1059: Obviousness of claims 2-14, 16-31, 33-52, 56-59, 84-88, 90 and 93 over Leverenz and other art; Board obviousness ruling affirmed
we affirm the Board's finding that claims 2–14, 16–31, 33–52, 56–59, 84–88, 90 and 93 would have been obvious.
1076: Obviousness of '764 patent claims over Koga and Ryu; district court finding that Koga's sucking channel is not a thermal exchange chamber upheld, so claims are nonobvious.
sufficient evidence supports the district court’s finding that a person of ordinary skill in the art would not consider Koga’s “sucking channel” to be a “thermal exchange chamber.”
1106: Obviousness of the asserted claims of the '649 and '924 patents; Sports Tutor failed to prove obviousness by clear and convincing evidence, so the claims were not shown obvious.
We affirm the judgment of the district court that Sports Tutor did not meet its burden to prove the asserted patents were invalid as obvious.
1116: Obviousness of the '383 patent claims over Grulke, Drews II and Bales; jury finding of nonobviousness affirmed
This is sufficient to affirm the district court's determination that Zimmer did not show, by clear and convincing evidence, that the '383 patent's claims were obvious.
1132: Obviousness of the '993 patent claims; Appellants failed to prove them invalid as obvious, affirmed on reinstatement of the panel opinion.
We further affirm the Commission’s conclusions that Suprema infringes the ’993 patent, and that Appellants failed to prove invalidity of the ’993 patent.
1149: Obviousness of claims 10, 14 and 17 over Aumayer, Evans and Wendt
Claim 10 would have been obvious over Aumayer, Evans, and Wendt because it encompasses the analog embodiment of the invention discussed in the specification.
1196: Obviousness of claims 1-23 of the '828 patent over CN '550, Naggar and Pawelczyk; Board found claims not shown obvious and Federal Circuit affirmed.
1265: Obviousness of claims 1, 4, 8, and 10 over Florin in view of JP '634, under the narrower constructions; court affirmed the Board's obviousness rejection.
we agree that claims 1, 4, 8, and 10 would have been obvious over the combination of Florin and JP ’634.
1266: Obviousness of claims 7, 9, and 17; obviousness rejections vacated and remanded for the Board to reconsider under the correct claim constructions, without a merits ruling.
we vacate and remand the obviousness rejections of claims 7, 9, and 17 for proceedings consistent with this opinion
1279: Obviousness of claims 20-22 over Guyot in view of RFC 1635; Board found obvious and the court affirmed.
Therefore, we affirm the Board's finding that claims 20–22 would have been obvious in view of Guyot and RFC 1635.
1280: Obviousness of claim 15 over Guyot in view of Robinson; Board found obvious and the court affirmed in a footnote.
We affirm the Board's finding that claim 15 would have been obvious based on Guyot and Robinson, which B.E. does not challenge.
1283: Obviousness of claims 4 and 11 of the '581 patent over PCT '015; the court held the claims nonobvious because a skilled artisan would not have modified the two-compartment prior art to a single compartment with the claimed amounts.
Because it was not obvious to load the claimed concentrations of progestogenic compounds and estrogenic compounds in one compartment, we reverse the district court's finding of invalidity.
1361: Obviousness of claims 4-7 and 18-21 over Wesinger combined with RFC 2543, including whether the references teach away from each other.
VirnetX's arguments do not demonstrate a lack of substantial evidence in support of the PTAB's obviousness findings.
1423: Obviousness of claims 43, 71 and 86 over prior art (Poulton; Root/Teller); PTAB affirmed rejection as obvious
On this basis, we can "reasonably discern" that the PTAB determined that it would have been obvious to a PHOSITA to configure Root's electronic display to include VR, as taught by Poulton
1456: Obviousness under §103 of claims 16, 17, 19, 20 of the '096 patent over Hill and Finseth; court held the references do not teach away and affirmed unpatentability
we conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's fact finding that the prior art does not teach away from the claimed combination.
1495: Obviousness of claims 1, 2, 4, 5 of the '573 patent and claim 1 of the '440 patent over CompuSonics references, including rejection of commercial success nexus
We see no error in the Board's conclusion that claims 1, 2, 4, and 5 of the '573 patent and claim 1 of the '440 patent would have been obvious.
1496: Obviousness of claims 64 and 95 of the '440 patent requiring a hard disk, no teaching away
the Board did not err in concluding that claims 64 and 95 of the '440 patent would have been obvious.
1501: Obviousness of claims 1-13 and 19 over Selker in view of Grenda, Sharkey, or Manges; PTAB obviousness finding affirmed, and secondary considerations held insufficient to establish nonobviousness.
