6468: '320 patent claims 8 and 19 held obvious over Nordskog in view of Beaulieu; jury verdict supported by substantial evidence.
Substantial evidence supported the jury's verdict.
6497: Obviousness of '245 patent claims 1-15, 17, 18 (Board found not unpatentable; Facebook appealed and lost).
We therefore affirm the Board's holding that claims 1–15, 17, and 18 of the ’245 patent are not unpatentable as obvious over the asserted prior art.
6498: Obviousness of '657 patent claims 189, 334, 342, 348, 465, 580, 584, 592 (Board found unpatentable; Windy City cross-appealed motivation to combine Roseman and Rissanen and lost).

6499: Obviousness of '552 patent claims 1, 4, 6, 8, 9, 18-58 (Board found not unpatentable; Facebook appealed and lost).

6500: Obviousness of '552 patent claims 2, 3, 5, 7, 10-17, 59, 64 (Board found unpatentable; Windy City cross-appealed and lost).

6502: Obviousness of '356 patent claims 1-9, 12, 15-28, 31, 34-37 (Board found unpatentable; Windy City cross-appealed and lost).
We therefore affirm the Board’s holding that claims 1–9, 12, 15–28, 31, and 34–37 of the ’356 patent are unpatentable as obvious over the asserted prior art.
6506: Obviousness of claims 1-2, 4-16, 19, 25, and 27-31 over Middle in view of Kaplan, Saadat, or Spear; affirmed.

6507: Obviousness of claims 1-14, 19, 25, and 27-31 over Kaplan in view of the knowledge of a skilled artisan; affirmed.

6581: Obviousness of claims 1-4, 6-7, 9-16, 18 of the '731 patent over Shinozuka and Sackier (and related claims over Nishioka): Board found unpatentable; affirmed.

6613: Obviousness of claims 1 and 4-15 over McClelland, Kranz, Dixit and Howell, including motivation to combine and objective indicia; claim 15 stands with claims 1 and 4-14

6617: Obviousness of claim 6 of the '058 patent over Carter, Walker and the Slot Payouts Webpage; Board found petitioner failed to prove obviousness, affirmed as supported by substantial evidence

6644: Obviousness of the claimed 40mg glatiramer acetate three-times-weekly dosing regimen, including obvious-to-try and motivation to combine dose and frequency.

6645: Obviousness of the improved tolerability and reduced frequency of injection site and post-injection reactions limitations in the '250 and '413 patents (claims 7, 14, 15, 16, 17).

6646: Obviousness of the reduced severity of injection site reactions limitations in the '776 patent claims.

6656: Obviousness of challenged claims 6, 11, 16, 20 over Bowie, ADSL Standard and Vanzieleghem; substantial evidence supports obviousness.

6712: Obviousness of claims 1-17 of the '487 patent over Hart and Schering-Plough, affirmed based on the claim construction

6737: Obviousness of claims 1-3, 5, 14, 16, 17 and 19 of the '376 patent over Maes and Ransom, including the responding limitation and motivation to combine

6739: Obviousness of claims 1-6, 9 and 13 of the '465 patent over Maes and Ransom, including the mapping and sending limitations and motivation to combine

6746: Obviousness of '358 Patent claims 1-5 over the '928 Application alone and in combination with MTOS; Board's nonobviousness finding affirmed

6747: Obviousness of '072 Patent claims 1-4 over the '928 Application and MTOS based on the Derotation Tool limitation; Board's nonobviousness finding affirmed

6762: Obviousness: motivation to combine Kossmann, Branch and Koros, where the Board's finding of motivation was held supported by substantial evidence and affirmed (obvious).

6764: Obviousness: whether Kelleher's nerve-monitoring can detect the iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves, a specific Board theory the court remanded as a new finding that NuVasive had no adequate chance to address.
we remand this very narrow issue to the Board.
6834: Obviousness of claims 1-11 over SMIL 1.0 in light of the skilled artisan's general knowledge (pipelining), including reliance on the patent's own admissions and substantial evidence review; affirmed as obvious.

we conclude that the Board did not violate § 311(b) or the inter partes review statute in determining that the claims would have been obvious over SMIL 1.0 in light of the general knowledge of a skilled artisan.
6837: Obviousness of claims 1-21 and 25-39 of the '711 patent over the combination of Lelong and Uehira; Board's nonobviousness finding affirmed, with the court finding no reversible error in its treatment of the Fantone declaration, the claim 1 offset reading, and the motivation to combine.

6842: Obviousness: Board's rejection of Amazon's obviousness ground for failure to prove the 'sessions' limitations, so the claims are not shown obvious.
Amazon also objects to the Board's ultimate rejection of its anticipation and obviousness challenges... We agree.
6846: Obviousness of claims 1 and 17 of the '842 patent over Tymes; Board's finding affirmed under substantial evidence.
we affirm the Board's determination that the challenged claims would have been obvious in view of Tymes
6850: Obviousness of claim 11 over Sitrick, including the data entry device, spatially matching, pixel selection and motion vector limitations; Board found claim 11 obvious and court affirmed.
We affirm the Board's order with respect to that claim.
6870: Obviousness of independent claims 1 and 5 over Law and Dua, including motivation to combine and substantial evidence on the communications link limitation
we affirm the Board's finding of a motivation to combine the references, and hence the obviousness of claims 1 and 5.
6871: Obviousness of dependent claim 19 (device identifier comparison) over Law and Dua

6893: Obviousness of asserted claims 3-5, 13, 24-28, 31, 34 over McFarlane in combination with other references; PTAB found not obvious and Federal Circuit affirmed substantial evidence support.

6903: Obviousness of claim 13 of the '905 patent over Prohaska and Hoyler (end caps limitation; Board finding of obviousness upheld on substantial evidence)

6906: Obviousness of claim 1 of the '698 patent over Appel '770, Appel '551 and Arai (force and curvature limitations, motivation to combine, teaching away, secondary considerations)

6915: Obviousness of claims 1 and 6 of the '389 patent over Bertoncino and Foley, including whether Bertoncino taught the 'significantly lower' limitation under substantial evidence review. Board found obvious; affirmed.

6926: Obviousness of claims 11-13 of the '398 patent; court reinstated jury verdict that claims were nonobvious, reversing JMOL of invalidity.

6942: Obviousness of claims 10 and 11 over Donnelly and Iwamoto, based on the Board's claim construction; the Board's obviousness finding was affirmed.

6956: Obviousness: Johnson inherently teaches the terminal identifier limitation; Board's inherency finding not supported by substantial evidence, but error harmless.
We agree with Vivint that the Board erred in finding that Johnson inherently teaches the terminal identifier limitation and hence supports a conclusion of obviousness.
6957: Obviousness: Moriya's model code teaches the terminal identifier limitation, supported by substantial evidence.
We therefore conclude that the Board's finding that Moriya teaches the terminal identifier was supported by substantial evidence.
6958: Obviousness: Johnson teaches the 'generating second control information' limitation, supported by substantial evidence.

6981: Obviousness of asserted claims 1-6; no reasonable expectation of success in combining Weiss, Chapman, Rapoport and FDA communications, so claims nonobvious

6992: Obviousness of claims 12, 15, and 32 (interference fit limitation): Polygroup did not prove unpatentability because Korengold does not teach an interference fit; affirmed.

6993: Motivation to combine DeVicaris with Korengold: Board erred in finding no motivation; Polygroup established a sufficient motivation, so the unpatentability determination for the remaining claims was vacated and remanded.

7006: Obviousness of ’615 claims 1-5 and claim 10 (invalidated as obvious over Reuter and Sanfilippo); Board ruling affirmed.

7007: Nonobviousness of ’615 claims 6-7 (fourth concave side); Board's ruling upholding them affirmed.

7235: Fluid Patents held nonobvious over Johnson and Karabinus references because coordinated fluid introduction was not taught

7273: Obviousness of cross-appealed claims 9-10 over Bannuscher and Truppe. Board found petitioners did not show unpatentability and the Federal Circuit affirmed.

7333: Obviousness of claims 2, 3 and 5 of the '925 patent; jury verdict of obviousness upheld under substantial evidence, including motivation to combine and rejection of teaching-away and secondary-considerations arguments.

7348: Obviousness of dependent claims (22, 36, 37, 42, 44, 45 and 70, 71, 74) over Kenoyer; affirmed because Microsoft did not separately argue obviousness

We thus affirm the Board's conclusion that claim 1 was not shown to be unpatentable for obviousness over Kontos alone.
7985: Obviousness of claim 1 over the combination of Kontos and Adams: the Board found a skilled artisan would not have combined them, and the court affirmed nonobviousness.
We thus affirm the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would not have combined Kontos and Adams (and the overall conclusion of nonobviousness based on that finding).
8013: Obviousness of claims 1-7 of the '186 patent. The Board had found a motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success but held the claims not unpatentable based on secondary considerations. The court held the secondary-consideration evidence lacked nexus under the proper legal standard and reversed the Board's nonobviousness judgment.
The Board’s judgment that claims 1–7 of the ’186 patent are not unpatentable must therefore be reversed.
8021: Obviousness of claim 3 (object field including a digitized audio file) over Zydney; Board's finding that Zydney renders claim 3 obvious was supported by substantial evidence and affirmed.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding about Zydney's teaching related to claim 3
8022: Obviousness of claim 24 (connection object messages) over Zydney and Hethmon; Board's finding of a sufficiently motivated combination, and rejection of Uniloc's teaching-away argument, affirmed.
Substantial evidence likewise supports the Board's finding that the "connection object messages" limitation of claim 24 is taught by the sufficiently motivated combination of Zydney and Hethmon.
8028: Obviousness: Board held claims 3-19, 21, 24-32 and 34 obvious over combinations of Anderson, applicant admitted prior art, Fried, Yeh, Son and Katada, including motivation to combine, level of skill and claim 9 limitations.
Accordingly, substantial evidence supports the Board's conclusions as to obviousness.
8033: Obviousness of dependent claims 3 and 16 over Knip; Board legally erred in enablement analysis of prior art reference, so obviousness finding reversed
Because the relied-upon prior art fails to enable a skilled artisan to make and use the claimed invention, we reverse.
8053: Obviousness of the ’709 patent claims and proposed substitute claims over Rae and the German patents DE759 and DE230, including the rotatable support and hat channel limitations. The Board's finding was affirmed under substantial-evidence review.
With respect to the Board’s reliance on the prior art references, however, we conclude that the Board’s decision was supported by substantial evidence, and we therefore affirm.
8067: Obviousness of challenged claims of the '614 patent over Burren, Venezia and de Gennes; Board's finding that de Gennes is analogous art was unsupported by substantial evidence because petitioner did not argue analogousness to the challenged patent.
Because Mylan argued that de Gennes is analogous to another prior art reference and not the challenged patent, Mylan did not meet its burden to establish obviousness premised on de Gennes.
8071: Obviousness of claims 1-15 of the '290 patent over Steigerwald '090 and Pressman, including whether a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine the references
Accordingly, substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine Steigerwald '090 and Pressman.
8072: Objective indicia (secondary considerations): no nexus between SynQor's commercial success, skepticism, adoption and praise evidence and the claimed combination
We agree with the Board that SynQor's secondary considerations evidence is not tied to the claimed combination of features in the '290 patent
8107: Obviousness of claims 1-9 and 12: Board's nonobviousness determination vacated and remanded because it rested on the inadequate claim construction.
we vacate the Board's construction of the term 'hardware buffer,' its determination that claims 1-9 and 12 were non-obvious over the prior art
8115: Obviousness: whether the asserted prior art combination discloses the 'disposed over' limitation of claim 1; court held the prior art discloses it, reversing the Board.
We therefore hold that the asserted prior art discloses the “disposed over” limitation from claim 1 in each challenged patent.
8116: Obviousness: whether the operating manuals disclose the 'stop gate' limitation; court found the Board's nondisclosure finding unsupported by substantial evidence and reversed. The overall unpatentability conclusions were vacated and remanded.
Thus, we reverse the Board’s finding.
8128: Obviousness of claim 13 over Stubbs and Kent: Board found the routing limitation not taught by Stubbs, so claim 13 is patentable
We conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Stubbs does not teach the "routing" limitation of claim 13.
8129: Obviousness of system claim 11 over Stubbs and Kent: incompatible communication protocols limitation not taught, so claim 11 is patentable
We conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's findings concerning these claims.
8130: Obviousness of claims 11, 15 and 16 over Grube and Shepherd: Grube inter-ward interface is not a group controller, so claims are patentable
substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Grube's inter-ward interface does not meet this definition.
8133: Obviousness of the One-French claims over Ressemann in view of Takahashi; Board found Medtronic failed to prove obviousness, including the intended-purpose-destruction motivation argument.
The Board did not err in determining Medtronic failed to carry its burden to show the One-French Claims would have been obvious, and substantial evidence supports its underlying findings of fact.
8134: Obviousness of the Double-Incline claims over Ressemann and Kataishi; Board found no motivation to combine.
We conclude the Board did not err in its analysis and that substantial evidence supports its findings.
8135: Obviousness of the substitute claims over Kontos in view of Kataishi and Takahashi; Board found no motivation to combine Kataishi and Kontos.
Medtronic does not challenge the factual bases for these findings. Accordingly, we affirm on this ground
8139: Obviousness: Board's motivation-to-combine finding over Kaulbach, including teaching-away analysis, held unsupported by substantial evidence; obviousness conclusion reversed.

We hold that the Board relied on an inadequate evidentiary basis and failed to articulate a satisfactory explanation that is based on substantial evidence for why a POSA would have been motivated to increase Kaulbach's melt flow rate to the claimed range
8140: Objective indicia: Board erred by finding no nexus between the claimed invention and commercial success because individual limitations were disclosed in the prior art.
Contrary to the Board's decision, the separate disclosure of individual limitations, where the invention is a unique combination of three interdependent properties, does not negate a nexus.
8141: Objective indicia: Board erred in requiring market share data to show commercial success; sales data alone can suffice.
However, market share data, though potentially useful, is not required to show commercial success.
8142: Objective indicia: Board misapplied the blocking-patents doctrine by treating the challenged patents themselves as blocking patents.
However, the challenged patent, which covers the claimed invention at issue, cannot act as a blocking patent.
8150: Obviousness: the Board's finding of no motivation to combine the Feasibility Study with Lee was reversed; the court held the claims obvious, applying the wrong legal requirement that both references teach carrier aggregation and that Lee's particular circuitry be shown necessary.

The evidence of record clearly shows a skilled artisan would have been motivated to achieve the benefits of carrier aggregation with a multi-LNA receiver like Lee's. Accordingly, we reverse the Board's finding of no motivation to combine.
8161: Obviousness under pre-AIA §103 of pending claims 1 and 12-16 over Hu, Gardner and Drayson; the court held the Board's finding that Hu teaches placing the overlay module on the third device was supported by substantial evidence and affirmed the rejection.
The Board's finding therefore is supported by substantial evidence.
8171: Obviousness of claim 24 of the '969 patent over the Giordano and Wallace combination; Board found no motivation to combine and upheld patentability
We hold that the Board did not err and affirm.
8172: Obviousness of claims 24-26 of the '969 patent over the Timm and Anderson combination; Board found insufficient motivation to combine and upheld patentability, supported by substantial evidence
substantial evidence supports the Board’s decision to uphold claim 24’s patentability over the Timm and Anderson prior art references.
8210: Obviousness of '151 patent claims 1-2, 6-8, 12-14 over Kiuchi in view of Rescorla; affirmed as consequence of anticipation affirmance.
Therefore, we also affirm the Board's conclusion that Kiuchi in view of Rescorla renders all challenged claims of the '151 patent obvious.
8218: Obviousness of claims 1-8 over Zydney and Clark (instant voice messaging application and message database limitation): Board's unpatentability finding affirmed.
we conclude therefore that Uniloc's argument is without merit and that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the references teach the instant voice messaging application limitation
8220: Obviousness of claims 9-12, 14-17, 25 and 26 over Zydney (attaches-to limitation): Board's unpatentability finding affirmed.
The Board's finding that Zydney discloses this limitation is supported by substantial evidence.
8226: Obviousness of claim 1 over RFID for Dummies; genuine dispute of fact precludes summary judgment of nonobviousness
We therefore reverse the district court's grant of summary judgment that RFID for Dummies does not anticipate or render obvious claim 1 and remand for a trial limited to claim 1's validity.
8262: Obviousness of original claims 6, 17-19 and 21 over Der and Valla: the court affirmed the Board's finding that a skilled artisan lacked motivation to combine, so the claims were not shown obvious.
We affirm the Board's claim construction and decision as to claims 6, 17–19, and 21.
8263: Obviousness of substitute claims 27, 28 and 31 over Der, Burgener and Razavi: the court held the Board's no-motivation-to-combine finding unsupported by substantial evidence, vacated, and remanded with instructions that Intel showed sufficient reason to combine.
we conclude that substantial evidence does not support the Board's determination that a skilled artisan would have lacked reason to combine Der with Burgener
8264: Obviousness of nucleotide analog claims ('852, '139, '358, '480 patents) and method claims ('985 patent) over Tsien, Prober, Dower and Metzker, including motivation to pursue allyl capping group and reasonable expectation of success
We agree with Illumina that the Board's conclusion was supported by substantial evidence.
8274: Obviousness: whether a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine Gifford with the Imtra references; Board found no motivation and the court affirmed.
the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would not have been motivated to combine Gifford with the Imtra 2011 and Imtra 2007 references is supported by substantial evidence.
8285: Obviousness of claim 5 over Tolman in combination with Surjaatmadja
in combination with Surjaatmadja, renders obvious claim 5.
8290: Obviousness of claims 1, 3-5, 11, 13-15 over Samsung combined with Dahlman or Nokia, including reasonable expectation of success; Board found obvious and Federal Circuit affirmed
The Board therefore did not err in concluding that independent claims 1 and 11 would have been obvious over Dahlman (or Nokia) together with Samsung and we affirm those holdings.
8294: Obviousness of claims 1-9 of the '149 patent (deuterated ruxolitinib analogs) over Rodgers, Shilling and the Concert Backgrounder, including motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success

We conclude that the Board had substantial evidence, including the testimony of Incyte's expert, Dr. Guengerich, to find that the combined teachings of Shilling, Rodgers, and the Concert Backgrounder would have provided a skilled artisan with motivation to deuterate ruxolitinib
8295: Objective indicia of nonobviousness (unexpected results and long-felt need) insufficient to rebut prima facie obviousness
Nothing about Sun's objective indicia evidence rebuts Incyte's prima facie showing of obviousness.
8297: Obviousness of claim 1 of the '228 patent over TexasBoars and Jeong, including motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success; Board found claims obvious and affirmed
Because the Board's findings are supported by substantial evidence, we affirm.
8298: Objective indicia of nonobviousness: Board's finding that no presumption of nexus applied to Jager Pro's commercial product was supported by substantial evidence
The Board's finding regarding nexus is supported by substantial evidence.
8316: Obviousness of claims 10 and 11 over Harada and other references; court found substantial evidence does not support finding that Harada teaches the controller limitation, so claims are nonobvious
substantial evidence does not support the Board's finding that Harada teaches the controller limitation.
8324: Obviousness of claims over the Gilhousen865 and Gilhousen390 combination (claim 22 of the '904 patent).
Substantial evidence supports the Board’s determination of obviousness based on the combination of Gilhousen865 and Gilhousen390.
8325: Obviousness of claims over Ito combined with CDMA references (including Gilhousen501 and Paneth combinations).
Substantial evidence supports the Board’s conclusion to the contrary.
8348: Obviousness of independent claim 11 of the '373 patent and claim 10 of the '419 patent over iOS User Guide and Griffin (with Davis); Board found claims not shown unpatentable and the court affirmed.
we affirm the Board’s decision finding independent claim 11 of the ’373 patent and independent claim 10 of the ’419 patent, and their dependent claims, were not shown to be unpatentable.
8365: Obviousness of the '304 patent under 35 U.S.C. 103; the jury could rely on the absence of evidence of motivation to combine, so the patent was not shown obvious.
a reasonable jury could have relied on the relative absence of evidence showing that a skilled artisan would have had a sufficient reason or motivation to combine the prior art references.
8386: Obviousness of claims 1-18 over Murphy and Guang; Board's finding affirmed as supported by substantial evidence
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the Murphy-Guang combination teaches shifting a convergence point, we affirm the Board's decision.
8396: Obviousness of claims 1 and 5 of the '504 patent and claims 5-7, 9, 10, 12, 49, 51 of the '505 patent over Herz, Zetts, Finkelstein; Board held claims obvious and Federal Circuit affirmed.
We affirm the Board's decisions that the challenged claims of the '504 and '505 patents are unpatentable for obviousness.
8400: Obviousness of original claims 1-11 over Strub combined with Nagai or Gleissner; objective indicia lacked nexus to the claimed invention.
Thus, the Board properly held claims 1–11 unpatentable for obviousness.
8403: Nonobviousness of substitute claims 15-28 over Strub and Wood, alone or with Nagai or Gleissner, based on weak motivation to combine Wood and strong objective indicia with presumed nexus.
We see no reversible error in the Board’s determinations that substitute claims 15–28 are not unpatentable for obviousness over Strub and Wood
8406: Obviousness: motivation to combine Kabemoto and Bauman under the known-technique rationale; Board finding reversed, motivation found.
Nothing more is required to show a motivation to combine under KSR, so we reverse the Board's finding to the contrary.
8407: Obviousness of claim 5 (chronological sequence limitation): remanded for the Board to address remaining patentability dispute.
But because the Board failed to analyze the invention of claim 5 as a whole, we must remand.
8425: Obviousness: Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine Grady with Ruchala's linac was supported by substantial evidence; claims held obvious.
We hold that the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine the Grady device with Ruchala's linac is supported by substantial evidence
8426: Obviousness: Board's implicit finding of a reasonable expectation of success in combining Grady and Ruchala was sufficient and supported by substantial evidence.
we hold that the Board made a sufficient, implicit finding that a skilled artisan would have had a reasonable expectation of success in combining the prior art references.
8440: Obviousness of claims 1-4 over Misselbrook in view of secondary references, including motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success

we hold that, despite the Chan teaching, the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to prepare acephate granules without a binding agent was supported by substantial evidence.
8453: Obviousness of the challenged claims over Barnhart in view of Gilbert, including the Board's definition of the person of ordinary skill in the art (POSA) and its access-to-expert language; the court held the POSA definition not erroneous and found the obviousness determination supported by substantial evidence.
We find that the Board's obviousness determinations are supported by substantial evidence.
8459: Obviousness of claims 1-4 of the '568 patent over Ogino alone; Board found Ogino teaches TTL less than EFL and that center-to-edge thickness limitations would have been obvious; affirmed

We rely on our discussion in the 20-1424 Decision to affirm the Board's ruling that Ogino teaches a TTL less than EFL. That conclusion requires affirmance of the obviousness conclusion as to claims 1–4 here.
8460: Obviousness of claim 5 over Ogino in combination with Beich, including whether a relevant artisan would have been motivated to apply Beich's center-to-edge thickness rule of thumb; affirmed

We also affirm the Board's conclusion of obviousness of claim 5 based on the determination, which is supported by substantial evidence, that a relevant artisan would have been motivated to make the combination of Ogino and Beich that meets the limitations of the claim.
8461: Obviousness of claims 1-20 of Nicira's application over Allen in view of Lin and Harjula; the Board's rejection was affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
The Board correctly interpreted representative claim 1 and properly affirmed Examiner's rejections of claims 1-20.
8475: Obviousness of the '595 patent security agent limitation over Gordon: substantial evidence supports Board finding that Gordon's host agent and firmware agent render the limitation obvious.

Because the Board's merits finding as to Gordon was supported by substantial evidence, we need not decide whether its forfeiture determination was an abuse of discretion, nor consider CUPP's argument regarding Joseph.
8498: Obviousness of claims 1-24 over Schlegl and Hevehan; Board held obvious, Federal Circuit held Apotex failed to demonstrate unpatentability, so claims nonobvious.
we hold that Apotex failed to demonstrate that claims 1–24 of the '138 patent are unpatentable under § 103(a).
8499: Obviousness of claim 15 of the '994 patent over Webster and Melby combination; Board found claim unpatentable, affirmed.
8504: Obviousness of reexamined claims 17-22 and 24-27 over Kossmann, Kelleher, Branch and Koros, including motivation to combine and objective indicia of nonobviousness; Board's obviousness conclusion affirmed.
Thus, we agree with the Board's ultimate legal conclusion that claims 17–22 and 24–27 would have been obvious.
8521: Obviousness of challenged method claims of the '118, '249, '498 and '250 patents over the prior art, including weighing of objective indicia on remand; Board found claims obvious and was affirmed.
We affirm the Board's holding that the asserted claims in the patents in suit would have been obvious over the prior art.
8556: Obviousness of claims 3, 14, 18, and 21 over Oinonen and Whitley
We affirm the Board's ruling that these claims are unpatentable as obvious.
8557: Obviousness of claims 20 and 22 over Oinonen, Whitley and Menard
We affirm that claims 20 and 22 are obvious over the combination of Oinonen, Whitley, and Menard
8567: Obviousness: motivation to combine Kiekhaefer and Brandt. Board's finding supported by substantial evidence despite its reliance on an employee's non-POSITA testimony.
The Board's finding of a motivation to combine is therefore supported by substantial evidence.
8568: Secondary considerations: nexus between objective indicia and the claimed invention. Board's finding of no nexus not supported by substantial evidence; nexus held shown.
We hold that Volvo Penta demonstrated a nexus between the claims and its evidence of secondary considerations.
8569: Weight assigned to objective indicia: copying and commercial success weights and long-felt need evaluation found not supported by substantial evidence.
In light of the Board's own findings that copying occurred, its assignment of only some weight was not supported by substantial evidence.
8607: Obviousness of claims 1-4, 6-14, 16-21 of the '088 patent over Apfel; the Board's nonobviousness finding that Apfel does not disclose the comparing step was not supported by substantial evidence, so the court vacated and remanded without itself finding the claims obvious.
Because substantial evidence does not support the Board's factual findings, we vacate and remand.
8620: Obviousness of claim 47 over Moreau alone and of claims 57, 59, and 60 over Moreau in view of Babos; dependent claim 47 not shielded by claim 41's anticipation rejection.
we affirm the Board's determinations that claim 47 is obvious over Moreau and that claims 57, 59, and 60 are obvious over Moreau in view of Babos.
8623: Obviousness of claims 2-5, 10-12 and 16 over Tomalin and Nishioka; the Board's finding of obviousness was affirmed under substantial evidence review.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that claims 2–5, 10–12, and 16 would have been obvious in view of Tomalin and Nishioka.
8656: Obviousness of the original claims over Strub and Woo, including the master timecode generator limitation and Zaxcom's secondary-considerations evidence (industry praise and long-felt need) lacking nexus; claims held unpatentable.
the Board had substantial evidence to support its determination that Zaxcom's evidence of industry praise and long-felt need lacked a nexus to the claims.
8674: Obviousness of claims 1-25 of the '647 patent over Johnson; Board found not shown obvious, affirmed on substantial evidence that Johnson does not disclose the portioning limitation
the Board had substantial evidence to support its nonobviousness determination for the claims on appeal.
8678: Obviousness of claims 1-13, 19-23 and 29-30 over Pratt and Tanabe, including motivation to combine, reasonable expectation of success and copying as objective indicia
Considering all the evidence, we conclude that claim 1 would have been obvious to a relevant artisan
8679: Breakage claims 14-16, 18 and 24-28 not proved obvious; L'Oréal failed to show the breakage decreases were inherent in the Pratt/Tanabe combination
We also affirm the Board's determination that the breakage claims were not proved unpatentable.
8726: Obviousness of claims 16, 18, 22, 23, 28 of the '482 patent and claims 4, 7, 17, 18 of the '621 patent (liquid enalapril formulations); district court held obvious and court affirmed.
We see no legal error in the district court's obviousness determination and conclude that it was supported by substantial evidence.
8758: Obviousness of dependent claims 10-14 over Wendus and Moxon; Board's teaching-away finding and motivation-to-combine findings lacked substantial evidence, and claims-as-a-whole analysis was flawed.
we vacate the Board's decision and remand the case for further consideration because the Board lacked substantial evidence for its conclusions.
8772: Obviousness of claims 15-25 of the '132 patent over Gelb, Tivoli and Callaghan; the court affirmed the Board's finding that Gelb is analogous art because it is reasonably pertinent to a problem the patent identifies, which supports the obviousness holding.
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Gelb is analogous art, we affirm.
8776: Obviousness of the verification limitation of claims 1-13 and 22 over Alexander (and combinations); Board found nonobvious, Federal Circuit held the Board's finding unsupported by substantial evidence.
We conclude that the Board’s determination that Alexander does not teach the verification limitation is not supported by substantial evidence.
8777: Obviousness of the highlighting limitation over Alexander and Liff; Board found nonobvious, Federal Circuit held it obvious.
We conclude that the highlighting limitation would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art in view of Alexander and Liff.
8780: Obviousness of claims 7 and 8 of the '991 patent over Yamaguchi, ETSI, Zak and Wiatrowski; Board found Hytera failed to show unpatentability, and the court held the prior art must teach each step including the response to each condition in the selecting limitation
we agree with the Board's conclusion that the prior art does not teach or suggest all of the limitations in claims 7 and 8.
8825: Obviousness of claims 1 and 5-8 over Gutman in view of Shoemaker: the court affirmed the Board's finding, supported by substantial evidence, that a skilled artisan would not have been motivated to combine the references, so the claims are nonobvious.
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would not have been motivated to combine those references, we affirm.
8828: Obviousness of claims 43, 44 and 46 over Carol-1995 and Viggars, including level of ordinary skill (formal computer programming experience), motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success; Board's unpatentability finding affirmed.
we affirm the Board's determination that claims 43, 44, and 46 are unpatentable as obvious.
8834: Obviousness of all claims of the '814 patent over Hassan and Birzl; Board's motivation-to-combine finding supported by substantial evidence, and Board's conclusion affirmed.
Because the Board's findings are supported by substantial evidence and the Board did not abuse its discretion, we affirm.
8843: Obviousness of claim 3 of the RE604 patent (method of treating Non-24 with 20 mg tasimelteon), based on Hack, the '244 publication, Lankford and Hardeland; includes reasonable expectation of success and rejection of Vanda's objective indicia arguments.
In sum, we find no error in the district court's determination that claim 3 of the RE604 patent is invalid for obviousness.
8844: Obviousness of claim 5 of the '487 patent (administering tasimelteon without food), decided as obvious to try given FDA food-effect guidance and a binary choice of options.
Under these circumstances, given the FDA guidance, it would have been obvious to try administering tasimelteon without food.
8845: Obviousness of claim 4 of the '910 patent (discontinuing rifampicin before tasimelteon), based on ramelteon drug-interaction studies and Vachharajani and Hardeland.
We therefore find no error in the district court's finding that it was obvious to avoid coadministration of rifampicin and tasimelteon, and that claim 4 would have been obvious.
8846: Obviousness of claim 14 of the '829 patent (discontinuing a strong CYP1A2 inhibitor before tasimelteon), based on Hardeland's warning and the ramelteon-fluvoxamine study; obviousness requires only a reasonable expectation of success.
The district court did not err in finding that claim 14 would have been obvious.
8850: Obviousness: district court's finding that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine the prior art references (Davies/Kerr/Bahal and Strang/Kulkarni/Djupesland) was not clearly erroneous, so the asserted claims are obvious.
we hold that the district court’s finding that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine the asserted prior art references to arrive at the claimed invention is not clearly erroneous.
8851: Obviousness: whether the Wyse reference taught away from using benzalkonium chloride (BZK); the court held the prior art as a whole did not teach away and the district court applied no incorrect legal standard.
We therefore discern no clear error in the district court’s decision to afford less weight to Wyse’s findings in its teaching away analysis.
8852: Obviousness: objective indicia of nonobviousness (unexpected results, copying, industry skepticism, long-felt need, failure of others) were properly weighed and given little weight; long-felt-need error found harmless.
Based on the evidence presented at trial, we hold that the district court did not clearly err in its factual findings regarding a lack of unexpected results.
8862: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103 in the double patenting analysis: the court held the application claims obvious over the '871 claims, including inherency of the dosing limitation and rejection of the Rougeot Declaration's objective indicia (unexpected results and long-felt need).
Pasteur has not shown that this limitation would not be inherent when practicing the prior art method of the ’871 Patent as described by the Board.
8872: Obviousness of claims 3 (S-enantiomer) and 4 (crystalline monohydrate) over Edmondson, Bastin and Brittain: the Board found no motivation to combine and no reasonable expectation of success, and the court affirmed that the claims were nonobvious.

We agree with Merck that the Board's decision that Mylan failed to show that claims 3 and 4 of the '708 patent would have been obvious to a skilled artisan at the time the invention was made was supported by substantial evidence.
8874: Obviousness of claim 11 over the combination of BinGO and Reed.
Because that argument has been rejected for anticipation purposes, it fails a fortiori in the obviousness context.
8919: Obviousness of claims 1, 5, 6, 8-10, 14 and 19 over Longobardi and Devonshire; Board found no implicit disclosure of the blue light energy limitation and no proof that sufficiently powerful blue LEDs existed in 1992; Federal Circuit affirmed under substantial evidence review.

On this record, substantial evidence supports the Board's factual finding that Haag-Streit did not prove by a preponderance of the evidence that Longobardi implicitly discloses the "blue light energy" limitation of claims 1 and 15 of the '394 patent.
8958: Obviousness of IPR-challenged claims 31-55 of the '220 patent and 26-49 of the '232 patent over the IBM Technical Disclosure Bulletin; Board's finding that IBM discloses the measuring, storing and comparing torque limitations was supported by substantial evidence.
The Board's findings that the prior art disclosed the disputed claim limitations is supported by substantial evidence.
8961: Obviousness of the design patents over Linz: the court held Linz creates the same overall visual appearance as the claimed designs, so the claimed designs would have been obvious, and reversed the Board.
Because the claimed designs would have been obvious over Linz, we reverse.
8962: Objective indicia of nonobviousness: the court held the presumption of nexus did not apply because the iQ Maximizer was not coextensive with the claims, and that Gamon did not show nexus-in-fact for commercial success and praise, so those indicia did not rebut obviousness.
We therefore hold that, as in the utility patent context, objective indicia must be linked to a design patent claim's unique characteristics.
8979: Obviousness of claims 1-3, 6-10, 13-17, and 20 of the '407 patent over Vorbach; Board found them unpatentable as obvious and the Federal Circuit affirmed.
In the '989 IPR (Appeal No. 22-1430), we see no legal error in the Board's obviousness determination based on Vorbach and conclude that it was supported by substantial evidence.
8989: Obviousness: whether Golan is analogous prior art (same field of endeavor) and the Board's finding supported by substantial evidence.
We also find that substantial evidence supports the Board's findings with respect to Golan.
8998: Obviousness of claims 1-17 and 23-25 over Kalmanek; held obvious and unpatentable.
We affirm the Board's construction of 'intercepting' and the Board's related holding that claims 1-17 and 23-25 of the '552 patent are unpatentable.
8999: Obviousness of claims 18-22 over Kalmanek; Apple failed to show unpatentability because the petition relied on two separate messages, contrary to claim 18's single-message requirement (nonobvious).
We also affirm the Board's holding that Apple failed to demonstrate by a preponderance of the evidence that claims 18-22 are unpatentable.
9000: Obviousness of claims over Goldfarb; Board's obvious-to-try analysis under KSR upheld, claim element (leaflet clip coupled to annular portion via flaps) obvious
We conclude that the Board's findings made under this paragraph have substantial-evidence support and that its determination of obviousness is not legally erroneous.
9020: Obviousness of claim 1 over Krepshaw and Freeman, including reasonable expectation of success and unexpected results. The Board's determination that claim 1 was obvious was upheld.

Substantial evidence supports the Board's determination that Krepshaw discloses to a relevant artisan each limitation of claim 1 of the ʼ768 application other than the batter limitation, which is disclosed by Freeman.
9046: Obviousness of claim 1 of the '196 patent over Chardon and Mishra, including motivation to combine and secondary considerations; Roku failed to show clear and convincing evidence of obviousness.
Because Roku does not directly address or dispute any of the Commission's findings on obviousness, we affirm.
9066: Obviousness of ’588 patent claims over Chen, Lindahl and Hurst; Board found no proven reasonable expectation of success because it evaluated the combination with Chen's inventive system; court held this was a fundamental legal error and vacated and remanded.

The Board's redefinition, pervasively substituting a focus on Chen's own inventive "system" for the petition's focus on particular Chen disclosures about pre-Chen art, see Netflix, 2021 WL 3729361, at *6–11, was a fundamental legal error.
9072: Obviousness of claims 1-21 of the '134 patent over Wada and Barrett; the Board's finding of obviousness was affirmed under substantial evidence review.
We affirm that the ’134 patent was obvious over the combination of Wada and Barrett and conclude that the Board’s decision was supported by substantial evidence.
9074: Obviousness of the asserted LFT patent claims (dose reduction and reescalation for Grade 2 liver enzyme elevations) over Azuma, the Pirespa label, and standard medical practice.
We agree with Sandoz that the district court did not err in its conclusion of obviousness.
9086: Obviousness of claims 1 and 2 of the '673 patent over Muzik in view of Espinoza or Hanlon; Board found the suction line element not taught or suggested by the references.
We conclude that substantial evidence supports these findings.
9118: Obviousness of claim 1 downward-drainage (seam allowing moisture to seep away) limitation; Board's finding insufficient, vacated and remanded
We vacate the Board's obviousness determination and remand to the Board for such further proceedings as are appropriate.
