10151: Obviousness under §103 of claims 1-20 of the '052 patent over NetPack alone or combined with Boyle; Board held claims unpatentable and the court affirmed.

Because Mr. Driessen does not challenge the correctness of the Board's Final Written Decision independent of his forfeited arguments, we affirm the Board's determination that claims 1–20 are unpatentable.
10164: Obviousness of claims 1-9, 19 and 20 of the '471 patent over Layfield and Rinard, including motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success on the resilient strut limitation; the Board's obviousness finding was affirmed
we affirm the Board's determination that claims 1–9, 19, and 20 of the '471 patent are unpatentable as obvious.
10167: '1200 IPR: whether the claims would have been obvious over Hassibi. The Board's finding that Hassibi does not disclose the 'identifying a single biomolecule' limitation, so the challenged claims were not shown unpatentable, was affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
This evidence provides substantial-evidence support for the Board's finding that Hassibi does not disclose 'identifying a single biomolecule.'
10168: '1163 IPR: whether the claims would have been anticipated or obvious over Choumane (with Weisbuch). The Board's finding that Choumane teaches the disputed limitation, so the challenged claims were unpatentable, was affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
The Board therefore found that PacBio had shown unpatentability of the claims challenged in the '1163 IPR.
10169: Obviousness of claim 1 of the '559 patent over GSK-711 and Merck-086, including the result-effective variable doctrine and substantial evidence on the molecular weight limitation.
Accordingly, we conclude that the Board’s determination that claim 1 would have been obvious over the references was supported by substantial evidence.
10170: Obviousness of dependent claims 3 and 4, which add multiple additional serotype glycoconjugates, with a reasonable expectation of success.

Substantial evidence therefore supports the Board’s conclusion that the subject matter of claims 3 and 4 would have been obvious in order to increase the coverage of serotypes of pneumococcal vaccines.
10180: Unpatentability of '505 patent claims: substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Chauvel and Hughes disclose a resource tag buffer under the construction adopted; claims held unpatentable.
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the prior art discloses a "resource tag buffer," we affirm.
10182: Obviousness of claims 1-21 of the '552 patent and claims 1-20 of the '713 patent over Sourcefire, including whether Sourcefire teaches the determination limitations, motivation to combine, and objective indicia of nonobviousness; the Board found the claims obvious and the court affirmed.
We reject Centripetal's challenges to the Board's obviousness determination.
10192: Obviousness of claims 1-5 of the '123 patent over Van Horn in view of Collier and the AHRI Standard, including substitution rationale, motivation to combine, and objective indicia of nonobviousness.
we affirm the Board's decision finding claims 1–5 of the '123 patent unpatentable as obvious.
10194: Obviousness of claims 1, 3, 5 and 7 of the '853 patent over Chardon; the Board found Roku did not show that Chardon's list of command codes teaches a listing of two communication methods, and the court affirmed under substantial evidence review.

Because the Board's factual finding—that Chardon's listing of command codes did not teach or suggest a listing of communication methods—was supported by substantial evidence, we affirm the Board's decision that Roku has not shown that the challenged claims would have been obvious.
10233: Obviousness of dependent claims 6-8 of the '581 patent; Board properly found Apple's petition failed to show unpatentability because Apple did not include Ahonen in the grounds addressing those claims; affirmed.
We agree with MPH that the Board did not err in denying Apple's petitions as to claims 6–8 of the '581 patent.
10238: Obviousness of Side Opening Claims (claims of '032, '380 and '776 patents); Board found nonobvious based on objective indicia (nexus, copying, commercial success, praise, long-felt need) overcoming a close prima facie case; affirmed.
we agree with the Board's determination that Medtronic failed to prove the Side Opening Claims obvious by a preponderance of the evidence.
10239: Obviousness of One-French Claims; Board's finding of no reasonable expectation of success and no obviousness upheld under substantial evidence review; affirmed.

we hold the Board's finding that Medtronic failed to establish a reasonable expectation of success to modify Kontos to achieve the One-French Claims was neither legally erroneous nor unsupported by substantial evidence.
10240: Obviousness of Double-Incline Claims of the '776 patent; Board's finding that kinking risk and objective evidence defeated obviousness; affirmed.
We therefore affirm the Board's determination that Medtronic failed to carry its burden to prove the Double-Incline Claims would have been obvious.
10248: Obviousness of claims 11 and 12: whether Pietraszak teaches the 'determining' limitation (Board finding supported by substantial evidence, claims obvious)
We agree with the Board that this teaching sufficiently discloses determining whether a new channel number is assigned to a source of programming.
10249: Obviousness of claims 11 and 12: whether Darbee teaches the 'in response to determining' limitation (Board finding supported by substantial evidence, claims obvious)
We agree and conclude that the Board's finding is supported by substantial evidence.
10283: Obviousness of claims 1, 3-4, 6, 8-9 of the '186 patent over Miller alone was not reached as contested; the court held Miller teaches every limitation of independent claims 10, 20, 28 ('186) and 1, 7 ('187) and dependent claims, so those claims are unpatentable as obvious/anticipated over Miller under the proper construction.

Under the proper construction, we conclude that Miller teaches every limitation of these claims and, therefore, that Polygroup has established the unpatentability of each independent claim challenged on appeal.
10295: Obviousness of independent claims 1, 14, 28, 40, 51, and 62 over Malik and Väänänen, including the transmitting-the-selected-recipients limitation, motivation to combine, and teaching away.

Accordingly, substantial evidence supports the PTAB’s finding that Malik and Väänänen rendered obvious the “transmitting the selected recipients” limitation recited in independent claims 1, 14, 28, 40, 51, and 62.
10308: Obviousness of claims 1-8, 10, 11 and 9, 12 over Ross (and Calder); Board found petitioner did not show unpatentability
For the foregoing reasons, we affirm the Remand FWD.
10327: Obviousness of claims 1, 7, 9, 10 over Cavallo combined with Bayliss; Board found unpatentable and court affirmed, including motivation to combine.
We therefore affirm the Board's determination that Cavallo combined with Bayliss renders claim 1 unpatentable for obviousness.
10336: Obviousness of claims 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7 of the '417 patent over Liu (alone, or with Gwon) and other references; Board found the claims unpatentable as obvious and the court affirmed.
We see no error in the Board's obviousness determination, which is supported by substantial evidence.
10377: Obviousness of proposed substitute claim 49 over Nishida, the Schuessler References and Spencer, including the Board-raised omitting-stitches theory and motivation to combine based on finite predictable solutions and minimizing waste.
the Board did not err in finding that substitute claim 49 is unpatentable as obvious and in denying Nike's motion to amend.
10435: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. § 103 of rejected claims 2 and 3 of application 15/711,381 over Niwamoto, Arling and Mui; Board found Arling teaches the tag file limitation and Niwamoto teaches the file name limitation, supported by substantial evidence.
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's findings, we affirm.
10450: Obviousness of all six claims of the '711 patent over Paulraj, Walton and Huang; Board found claims unpatentable as obvious, including claim construction under broadest reasonable interpretation underlying the obviousness finding
we affirm for the reasons stated by the Board.
10463: Obviousness of claim 14 (and related claims) over Giraud in view of Hagen; Board's finding of motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success affirmed under substantial evidence review.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that a person of ordinary skill in the art would have modified Giraud in view of Hagen to arrive at the claimed container.
10464: Obviousness of claim 29 over Giraud, Hagen and Moon, sustained by the Board for the same reasons as claim 14; not separately argued by CSP.

Finally, because CSP had not provided a separate argument for the Examiner's rejection of dependent claim 29, the Board sustained the rejection of this claim over the combination of Giraud, Hagen, and Moon for the same reasons it sustained the rejection of claim 14.
10467: Obviousness over Baker reference: Board found claims unpatentable under §103 because Baker teaches the drive server, decoder and portion-presenting limitations; affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
The Board's reasoning on these findings is supported by substantial evidence.
10482: Obviousness of the Pharmacokinetic Claims (claims 4 and 5 of the '866 patent): no motivation to combine the references was shown, so the claims were not invalid.

Based on the record before us, we do not discern any clear error made by the district court in finding no motivation to combine the asserted prior art references to arrive at the Pharmacokinetic Claims.
10484: Obviousness of the pH of the Backing Layer Claims (claims 9 and 20 of the '539 patent): inherency and the prior-art backing layer pH were not shown, so the claims were not invalid.
We find no clear error in the district court's findings and therefore affirm the district court's decision holding the pH of the Backing Layer Claims not invalid.
10486: Obviousness of the pH of the BEMA Layer Claims (claims 3 and 10 of the '866 patent; claims 8, 9, and 20 of the '843 patent): the district court applied an incorrect clear-and-convincing standard to secondary considerations of long-felt need and unexpected results, so the obviousness judgment was vacated and remanded.

Because the district court should have considered the secondary considerations evidence presented to it under the preponderance of the evidence standard, we vacate the district court's judgment regarding obviousness of the pH of the BEMA Layer Claims and remand.
10493: Obviousness of claims over Diab and Amano: Board's finding of no motivation to combine the references, supported by substantial evidence, so claims not shown obvious.
We conclude that the Board's finding of a lack of motivation to combine Diab and Amano is supported by substantial evidence.
10518: Obviousness of '530 and '309 patent claims; ALJ rejected invalidity contentions, affirmed.
We see no reversible error in the ALJ's decision (adopted by the Commission) with respect to the '530 and '309 patents.
10529: Whether claims 27-30 of the '123 patent would have been obvious over Morgan in view of general knowledge in the art.
Thus, we affirm the Commission's final determination with respect to the validity of the '123 patent.
10550: Obviousness of claims 1-3, 5-9, and 11 of the '676 patent over Keskitalo in view of Lindell; Board found no motivation to combine, affirmed.
Because substantial evidence supports that finding, we affirm the Board's decision.
10551: Board's finding that the Keskitalo-Lindell combination was not shown to be motivated (question of fact, substantial evidence) and its understanding of petitioner's proposed combination.
We see no error in the Board's understanding of Appellants' proposed combination.
10557: Obviousness of claims of the '069, '044 and '486 patents over Steenfeldt-Jensen; Board's motivation-to-modify and substantial-evidence findings affirmed, claims held unpatentable as obvious.

The Board had substantial evidence to support its determination that, based on the express teaching of a nut member on the first embodiment of Steenfeldt-Jensen (at col. 7, lines 41–47), a relevant artisan would have modified the fifth embodiment with an internally threaded driver tube to engage the piston rod.
10576: Obviousness of claims 1-3 and 10 over Giamalva combined with Adams, including motivation to combine, reasonable expectation of success, and rebuttal of the prima facie case; the court affirmed the Board's obviousness rejection.
Those findings are supported by substantial evidence.
10588: Obviousness of claims 1-18 over Bock, Kiani and Woehrle; Board's obviousness finding supported by substantial evidence, favoring petitioner
This all amounts to substantial evidence for the Board's conclusion that a POSITA would have been motivated to combine Bock and Woehrle.
10595: Obviousness of claims 45-58, 60-74, 76-90, and 92 of the '088 patent (resolved by treatment of claim 45): Board's nonobviousness finding vacated because it rigidly required express disclosure of storing two syringes in one compartment.
We agree with Bard that the Board's decision was erroneous.
10596: Obviousness of claims 1-2, 6-10, 16-19, and 25-44 of the '088 patent (claims 1 and 25 treatment): Board's nonobviousness finding vacated for overly rigid obviousness analysis of the syringe-height limitation.
We agree with Bard that the Board's decision was erroneous. As the Board found, Serany discloses grouping like items together in a single compartment
10597: Obviousness of claims 7-8 and 11-13 of the '596 patent (claim 7 fluid receptacle under catheter): Board's nonobviousness finding vacated.
We agree with Bard. As before, the Board imposed anticipation-like requirements on the prior art in determining obviousness.
10598: Obviousness of claims 9-10, 14-16, and 21-22 of the '596 patent (claim 9 lubricant-receiving compartment): Board's nonobviousness finding affirmed under substantial evidence.
We agree with Medline on this issue that the Board's determination was supported by substantial evidence.
10599: Obviousness of claims 1-19 and 22-25 of the '761 patent (claim 10 lubricating jelly application chamber): Board's nonobviousness finding affirmed; any error on other limitations was harmless.
we affirm the Board's decision that claims 1–19 and 22–25 of the '761 patent, all of which are resolved by the above treatment of claim 10, are not unpatentable as obvious.
10601: Obviousness of claims of the '881, '211, and '649 patents over cited prior art; Board held claims unpatentable as obvious and Federal Circuit affirmed by incorporating companion opinion.
holding that the claims of U.S. Patents 9,346,881 (’881 patent), 9,890,211 (’211 patent), and 8,597,649 (’649 patent) are unpatentable because they would have been obvious over the cited prior art.
10613: Obviousness over Barnes in view of Janky: Board's finding that a skilled artisan would not have been motivated to combine the references was supported by substantial evidence, so claims were nonobvious.
The Board's finding that an artisan would not have been motivated to combine Barnes and Janky was thus supported by substantial evidence.
10618: Obviousness over Chen: substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Chen alone does not teach obtaining frames on the receive side before descrambling, so the challenged claims were not shown obvious on that ground.

We conclude, however, that substantial evidence supports the Board's determination that Chen does not teach or suggest obtaining 'frames' on the receive side before they are reassembled after descrambling.
10626: Unpatentability of claims 10, 11, 13, 17, 24 of the '698 patent and claims 1, 2, 4, 13-18 of the '196 patent as anticipated and/or obvious; affirmed because patent owner did not appeal merits beyond construction
we affirm the Board's conclusion that the challenged claims of the '698 patent and '196 patent are unpatentable.
10629: Obviousness of dependent claims 15-17 and 19 of the '816 patent; Board's finding of nonobviousness (Google failed to prove obviousness) affirmed because Google did not show error.

Google, who bears the burden on appeal, has failed to convince us that the Board’s determinations should be reversed. Accordingly, we affirm the Board’s determinations that claims 15–17 and 19 are not unpatentable.
10637: Unpatentability of claims 1-7 as determined by the Board in the final written decision; affirmed, with the Board's claim constructions controlling the outcome.
We affirm the Board's claim constructions and its final written decision determining that claims 1–7 are unpatentable.
10676: Whether the asserted claims would have been obvious over Pedicini in combination with other references; the ALJ found Pedicini lacks a distinct main storage chamber and the claims nonobvious, which the court affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
The ALJ’s analysis is supported by substantial evidence and is consistent with the agreed-upon construction.
10709: Obviousness of claims 1, 7, and 11-14 over Parienti in view of Goldsmith (grounds 5 and 6): the court held the Board erred and that Intex proved obviousness; the Board's nonobviousness conclusion was vacated and remanded for objective indicia and claim 5 analysis.
We conclude that the Board erred in determining that Intex failed to prove claims 1, 7, and 11–14 obvious.
10718: Obviousness/invalidity determination of the patents at issue, affirmed as flowing from claim construction and factual findings; the court's invalidity ruling was affirmed without separate analysis.
We also find no error, and certainly no clear error, in the district court's findings of fact, including its expert witness credibility determinations.
10728: Obviousness of claims 1-7, 10-14, 16-20 and 23-26 over Whitman and Tierney: Board's no-motivation-to-combine finding not supported by substantial evidence, so the claims are held unpatentable and the Board's non-obviousness determination reversed.
we reverse the Board's finding that claims 1–7, 10–14, 16–20, and 23–26 are not unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
10729: Obviousness of substitute claims 58-64 of the '486 patent over Steenfeldt-Jensen with Klitgaard, Atterbury and/or Burroughs (arc-shaped body and clicker claims).
Based on the record before us, we find that substantial evidence supports the Board's obviousness determination.
10740: Obviousness of asserted claims in view of Shafer as modified by Nakamura; district court's JMOL of nonobviousness reversed because a reasonable jury could find the claims obvious.
We hold that the district court erred in granting JMOL to Cyntec on the issue of nonobviousness.
10756: Whether claims 5 and 21 would have been obvious over Tada, given that LG's only disclosure of the claimed lens relied on the erroneous Table 5 values.

Because substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that prior art disclosure critical to both of LG's petitions for inter partes review was an apparent error that would have been disregarded or corrected by a person of ordinary skill in the art, we affirm.
10767: Obviousness of claims 1-7, 10, 12-17, and 20 of U.S. Patent No. 6,438,642 over Dibble and Cannon in the Dibble IPR, including whether Dibble teaches the 'different computer systems' limitation; the court affirmed the Board's finding that Dibble's LFSs are different computer systems, supported by substantial evidence.
Because we affirm the Board's unpatentability determinations in the Dibble IPR, we need not and do not reach the issues raised with respect to the Carter IPR.
10769: Obviousness of claims 4, 7, 15, and 18 over Linjama, Lehrma and Tosaki, including whether a reasonable expectation of success existed on remand

Dr. Abowd's testimony detailing the modified function of the code and that implementing such a modification would be "simple" and "straightforward" was sufficient to establish a reasonable expectation of success.
10778: Motivation and manner of combining Kiss and FIPA97 registries for claims 8-10 and 63 of the '115 patent and claim 28 of the '560 patent; Board's no-motivation finding held unsupported by substantial evidence
In these circumstances, we see no basis for a reasonable determination rejecting Microsoft's evidence of why and how the combination at issue would be made.
10782: Whether Microsoft showed that FIPA97 teaches the 'each registry resident within a separate computer process' limitation of claims 50-51 and 53-55 of the '560 patent; Board's finding that the petition failed to address the claim language affirmed
We affirm that determination, and thus we do not reach the parties’ dispute concerning the proper construction of “computer process.”
10786: Obviousness of claims 8 and 9 over Clarke (motivation to modify and reasonable expectation of success; Kushnir failure-of-others argument rejected)
In sum, we find that substantial evidence supports the facts underlying the Board's conclusion that claims 8 and 9 would have been obvious in light of Clarke.
10791: Obviousness of claims 2-4, 7, 9, 13, 27 and motivation to combine Nicol and Bhatia for claims 10 and 11; Board's no-motivation finding lacked substantial evidence, claims held obvious
We thus reverse the Board's finding on motivation to combine and accordingly determine that claims 10 and 11 are obvious.
10831: Obviousness of claims 18 and 19 under the 'aseptic' limitation: the prior art (Biewendt) and the FDA commercial-sterility standard render sterilizing bottles obvious.
These facts are enough to render obvious sterilizing bottles to meet the FDA's requirements for commercial sterility. We therefore affirm that portion of the Board's decision.
10832: Obviousness of increasing the prior-art sterilization rate from 100 to at least 101 bottles per minute, challenged for lack of substantial evidence.
That is substantial evidence in support of the Board's conclusion, which, consequently, we affirm.
10841: Obviousness of original claims 137-139 of the '474 patent over POH and James, including whether the prior art taught away and whether the combination was unsafe; the Board's finding of no copying (objective indicia) was affirmed.
We thus affirm the Board's determination that claims 137–139 of the '474 patent are unpatentable because they would have been obvious over the combination of POH and James.
10883: Obviousness under pre-AIA §103: the Board's finding that the Sikdar reference does not teach the 'dynamically isolating' limitation lacks substantial evidence, so Sikdar does teach that limitation under the agreed construction.
We conclude that the Board's finding is not supported by substantial evidence.
10905: Obviousness: Board found no motivation to combine Smith and Faraz; court held reliance on generic industry skepticism impermissible and vacated and remanded for reevaluation of motivation-to-combine evidence.
It follows that generic industry skepticism cannot, standing alone, preclude a finding of motivation to combine.
10961: Obviousness under §103 over the GyroWasher public use: the Board's finding that the claims were not shown obvious, resting on the same finding about liquid driven to the drain; affirmed.
we affirm the Board's final written decision holding that claims 1, 3–5, 7, 10–12, and 14–20 of the '063 patent were not shown to have been unpatentable in view of the asserted prior art.
10976: Obviousness of claims 1-11, 13-18 and 20 over Gilb '155, Bundy and Allan; Board found them obvious and the court affirmed.
Accordingly, we affirm the unpatentability of claims 1–11, 13–18, and 20 as obvious over Gilb ’155, Bundy, and Allan.
10978: Obviousness of substitute claim 40 on cross-appeal; Board found claim 40 nonobvious and the court affirmed.
Accordingly, we affirm the patentability of claim 40.
10981: Obviousness of '988 patent claims over Sugiyama in view of Gatto and Cheston; substantial evidence supports Board finding that Sugiyama teaches hardware and software fault inspection
We agree that substantial evidence supports the Board's factual findings underlying the unpatentability determinations for Sony's Sugiyama-based grounds.
10982: Obviousness of '670 patent claims over Sugiyama in view of Gatto (and Yamaguchi); substantial evidence supports Board findings

To the extent Bot M8 challenges the Board's findings that Sugiyama in combination with Gatto renders the claims of the '670 patent unpatentable as obvious, we conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's factual findings underlying its unpatentability determinations.
10992: Obviousness of thermostability dependent claims and Dassa/Greiner combinations: motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success found; claims obvious
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's determinations that the claims were obvious, we affirm.
10994: Obviousness of claims over Benning in view of Karami '626: Board's finding that the combination meets the relative retaining-force limitation was not supported by substantial evidence (inherency or obviousness), so the unpatentability ruling was vacated.
Whether the Board relied on inherency or obviousness, we agree with Hartmann that the Board erred in finding that Benning as modified by Karami '626 would meet the relative force claim limitation.
10995: Obviousness of claims over Benning in view of Karami '626: Board's finding that the combination meets the claimed over-abdomen retaining-force range limitations was unsupported and vacated.

Without such an admission or any other record evidence to support the Board's assertion ... the Board's analysis of whether the prior art combination discloses the claimed range limitations is unsupported and cannot stand.
10997: Obviousness over Miller alone of independent claims 10, 20, 28 of the '186 patent and claims 1 and 7 of the '187 patent and their dependents; court held Miller teaches every limitation, so the claims are unpatentable.

Under the proper construction, we conclude that Miller teaches every limitation of these claims and, therefore, that Polygroup has established the unpatentability of each independent claim challenged on appeal.
11010: Obviousness of claim 4 of the '631 patent over King and Arimilli; Board erred by requiring evidence of bodily incorporation and motivation to combine was shown as a matter of law, so claim 4 held obvious.
Based on the evidence before the Board, we hold that substantial evidence could only support a finding that an ordinary artisan would have been so motivated.
11024: Obviousness of claims of U.S. Patent No. 7,707,388 over Nakaya in combination with other references; the Board found no claim obvious and the court affirmed.
the Patent Trial and Appeal Board held that no claim of U.S. Patent No. 7,707,388 would have been obvious over Nakaya 1 in combination with other references. For the following reasons, we affirm.
11032: Obviousness of claim 1 of the '037 application over Fisher and Dresti, including motivation to combine and reliance on the combined references

We conclude that the Board’s factual determinations are supported by substantial evidence, and that the Board did not err in determining that it would have been obvious to a skilled artisan to combine the features of respective references
11033: Obviousness of claim 1 of the '095 application over Fisher and Meijer, including motivation to combine and reliance on the combined references

We conclude that the Board’s factual determinations are supported by substantial evidence, and that the Board did not err in determining that it would have been obvious to a skilled artisan to combine the features of respective references
11040: Claims 11 and 12 (and claim 12 of the '362 patent) not shown obvious over RFC3104 because the claimed source-address limitation was not disclosed under the Board's construction
Accordingly, we affirm the Board's holding that Apple failed to show those claims would have been obvious.
11042: Claims 4 and 5: Apple failed to show a motivation to modify the combination to use multiple fields, and the Board's rejection of Apple's expert testimony was affirmed
We see no use or endorsement of an erroneous obviousness standard in the Board's analysis.
11044: Claims 2 and 3: substantial evidence supported the finding that RFC3104's adding of a new header does not satisfy the substitution limitation and that no motivation to modify was shown
substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that RFC3104's disclosure of adding a new header does not satisfy the substitution required by the claims.
11046: Claims 9 and 10: the limitation recites an operation requiring an existing address field, so the combination did not teach it and the claims were not shown obvious
the limitation does not merely claim a result; it recites an operation of the intermediate computer that requires an existing address field.
11048: Claim 13 of the '362 patent and claims 14-16: Apple failed to show the combination taught an intermediate computer that updates an existing mapping
Apple failed to show the combination taught an intermediate computer that updates an existing mapping.
11049: Claims 7-9 of the '502 patent: substantial evidence supported the finding that RFC3104 does not teach signaling an address change, so the claims were not shown obvious
the Board's contrary finding is supported by substantial evidence, including MPH's expert testimony and RFC3104 itself.
11060: Obviousness: substantial evidence supports a motivation to modify Saidara by adding a noninvasive pulse oximeter to measure blood oxygen levels, so the claims are obvious.

Substantial evidence supports the Board’s findings that a skilled artisan would modify Saidara to noninvasively measure blood oxygen levels by adding a noninvasive pulse oximeter to Saidara’s sensor set.
11061: Obviousness: substantial evidence supports the finding that the prior art discloses multiple alarm delay or suspension periods of time for different parameters, as the independent claims require.
We disagree and conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board’s findings that the prior art discloses multiple alarm delay or suspension periods of time for different parameters.
11073: Obviousness of independent claim 1 (single event dose of 15-90 micrograms treprostinil) over the '212 patent in view of the Voswinckel abstracts
Accordingly, the Board's finding that the combination of the '212 patent, JESC, and JAHA would have rendered obvious claim 1 was supported by substantial evidence.
11074: Objective indicia of nonobviousness: unexpected results for claim 1 over the closest prior art (inhaled treprostinil)
With no other evidence to consider, we see no error in the Board's conclusion that UTC failed to satisfy its burden in establishing unexpected results.
11075: Obviousness of dependent claims 4, 6, and 7 (dry powder formulations, particles under 5 micrometers) based on the '212 patent, JESC and JAHA and expectation of success
In any event, the Board's conclusion that dependent claims 4, 6, and 7 were obvious was supported by substantial evidence.
11085: Obviousness of claims 1, 2, and 11 over Oda and other references; Board's unpatentability finding affirmed.
The Board therefore properly found that the Oda reference, in combination with other references cited to the Board, made claims 1, 2, and 11 unpatentable.
11099: Obviousness rejection of claims 9, 10, and 12-15 over the alleged public use combined with printed publications, affirmed because WinGen made no separate arguments on those claims.
Because WinGen makes no separate arguments with regard to the Board's affirmance of the examiner's rejection of claims 9, 10, and 12–15 as obvious, we likewise affirm the rejection of those claims.
11109: Obviousness of the challenged '297 claims over Bessler in combination with Johnson and other references; Board's obviousness finding reversed because St. Jude's theories did not meet the 'sized and shaped' limitation as properly construed
St. Jude's arguments regarding Johnson incorporate the error of its arguments regarding Bessler—they fail to meet the 'sized and shaped' limitation as properly construed.
11115: Obviousness of claims 1-16 of the '776 patent; Board found claims not shown obvious because asserted prior art only taught 0% duty cycle
Hence, it correctly concluded that the claims were not shown to have been obvious over the cited prior art.
11147: Obviousness of claims 7 and 10-14 where the Board failed to properly weigh objective indicia (commercial success and praise) by not addressing SandBox container-specific evidence; remanded for further analysis
Thus, failure to address the Sandbox container-specific evidence was legal error by the Board. On remand, the Board must consider this evidence to properly decide the issue of obviousness.
11151: Obviousness of claims 1-4 of the '152 patent over Border and Parulski; substantial evidence supports Board finding that Border discloses the point-of-view limitation
because substantial evidence supports the Board's determination, we affirm.
11159: Obviousness of claim 1 over Sie: no reasonable fact finder could find Sie teaches the available-to-a-user limitation, so claim 1 is nonobvious.
Thus, no reasonable finder of fact could find Sie teaches the available-to-a-user limitation.
11167: Obviousness of claims 13-15 and 17-18 of the '287 patent over Swayze in view of McInnis: the Board's finding that McInnis is analogous art (field of endeavor or reasonable pertinence) was supported by substantial evidence, so the reference was properly considered.
Based on the excerpts described above, we conclude that this finding was supported by substantial evidence.
11168: Obviousness of claims 13-15 and 17-18: the Board's motivation-to-combine finding, relying on the unrebutted Kastner reference, was supported by substantial evidence, so the claims are obvious.
The Board's motivation to combine finding is supported by substantial evidence in the form of an unrebutted reference (Kastner) and Intuitive's expert's declaration describing Kastner.
11186: Obviousness of claims 6-8, 11-13, 18-21 over Wu (Board found obvious; affirmed)
Substantial evidence thus supports the Board's findings on anticipation and obviousness of claims 6–8, 11–13, and 18–21 of the '473 patent over Wu.
11187: Obviousness of claims 9, 10, 14-17 over the combination of Wu and Sabat (including CPRI packetizing and motivation to combine; affirmed)
We affirm the Board's holding of obviousness over the combination of Wu and Sabat and need not address obviousness over Wu alone or Dali's arguments regarding Wu alone for these claims.
11196: Obviousness of the challenged independent claims of the '708 and '900 patents over Zou I combined with McNeely, Pease, or Pourahmadi; Board found no reasonable expectation of success, supported by substantial evidence, so claims nonobvious.

we affirm the Board's conclusion that Qiagen failed to demonstrate by a preponderance of the evidence that the challenged independent claims of the '708 and '900 Patents are unpatentable for obviousness
11201: Obviousness: substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Schmitt teaches non-uniquely tagged parent polynucleotides under the Board's construction.
We hold substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Schmitt teaches non-uniquely tagged parent polynucleotides and its finding regarding the reasonable expectation of success.
11202: Obviousness: substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have had a reasonable expectation of success in applying Schmitt's hybrid method to cfDNA.
We therefore hold substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have a reasonable expectation of success in using Schmitt's hybrid method to analyze cfDNA.
11203: Objective indicia of nonobviousness (nexus): Board's finding that Guardant360 is not coextensive with the claims rested on a clearly mistaken view of the evidence and a legal error in disregarding articles and expert testimony; the obviousness determination is vacated and remanded for further fact finding.
The Board erred as a matter of law in disregarding Guardant's evidence to establish a presumption of nexus.
11207: Analogous art under the field-of-endeavor test for Kaku as obviousness prior art; Board's finding that Netflix failed to identify the field of endeavor was vacated as an abuse of discretion for requiring magic words, and remanded.
We hold that the Board abused its discretion in requiring Netflix to explicitly identify the field of endeavor using specific language
11208: Analogous art under the reasonably pertinent test: substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Kaku addressed a different problem and is not reasonably pertinent, so Kaku is not analogous art.
We hold that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding.
11277: Obviousness of all claims of the '273 patent over Li, as determined by the Board on remand and affirmed.
the Board's determination that all claims of the '273 patent are unpatentable is affirmed.
11286: Obviousness of dependent claims 3-4 (and 6-7 as noted): the Board adequately articulated a reason to combine Foley and Plosker with a reasonable expectation of success, including the 75 and 81 mg aspirin dosages.
we see no failure by the Board to articulate an adequately supported rationale for why a skilled artisan would have combined Foley and Plosker with a reasonable expectation of success
11287: Secondary considerations: Bayer's unexpected-results evidence about clinical proof of efficacy lacked nexus to the claimed invention because it relied solely on the functionally unrelated limitation, so it did not compel nonobviousness.
Absent such nexus, we conclude Bayer's evidence of secondary considerations 'do[es] not compel a holding of nonobviousness.'
11295: Obviousness of claims 1-15, 17-25, 27-33 of the '675 patent over Yu in the Yu IPRs, including motivation to modify Yu for mobile devices and reasonable expectation of success
We agree with its conclusion that Intel proved that the claims challenged in the Yu IPRs are unpatentable.
11296: Chen IPRs: Board found Intel failed to show obviousness over Chen; Intel's cross-appeal on this ruling was not reached and dismissed
Given our conclusions regarding the Yu IPRs, and Intel's statements to us, we decline to address Intel's cross-appeal.
11299: Obviousness of the claimed AIBW dosing limitation, including motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success. The district court's finding of obviousness was not clearly erroneous and was affirmed.

11304: Obviousness of claims 1 and 10-12 over Himmelstein in view of Myr, including motivation to combine, and rejection of BillJCo's objective indicia (copying and commercial success) evidence; Board's unpatentability finding affirmed.
Substantial evidence therefore supports the Board's obviousness findings.
11326: Obviousness of claims 28-37 over Song '525 (obvious to try; affirmed)
The Board did not err in rejecting claims 28–37 as obvious over Song ’525.
11341: Obviousness of claims 1-20 over Nitz in view of Nykänen, including the teaching of claim 1[b], the teaching of claim 1[c] and motivation to combine. The Board's finding that the claims would have been obvious was affirmed under substantial evidence review.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding.
11357: Obviousness under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. § 103 of claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 8,656,419 over Verbeke (with other references for dependent claims); Board finding that Verbeke discloses the claimed limitations affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
CA may disagree with Dr. Jagadish's opinion, but his testimony constitutes substantial evidence to support the Board's finding.
11373: Obviousness of the claims over Chen, Lindahl and Hurst: under the adopted construction, limitation [l] is taught by the asserted prior art, so the challenged claims are unpatentable as obvious.
We hold, too, that limitation [l], so construed, is taught by the asserted prior art.
11374: Obviousness of claims 16-20 of the '585 patent over Works, Lindenman, and Fandrich, including motivation to combine and secondary considerations (nexus).
The Board found that there was a motivation to combine Works' gooseneck hitch system and Lindenman's fifth wheel hitch system, rendering claim 16 obvious.
11396: Obviousness of claims 1-22 of the '933 application over Buehler and He '660, including whether substantial evidence supports the Board's motivation-to-combine finding.
This is substantial evidence that supports the Board's motivation-to-combine finding.
11405: Obviousness of claims 1-5 of the '446 patent, claims 1-5 of the '019 patent and claims 1-11 of the '035 patent over Choi in combination with Kim or Noh, including motivation to combine and selection of Mg and Al within the claimed range.
the Board's decisions holding claims 1–5 of the ’446 patent, claims 1–5 of the ’019 patent, and claims 1–11 of the ’035 patent invalid as obvious are affirmed.
11425: Obviousness of all challenged claims (1-11, 13-19) over Ehlers or Ehlers in view of Chen; Board's holding affirmed.
The Board's determination of obviousness thus rests on a sound construction of claim 1.
11431: Obviousness of asserted claims of the '301, '262 and '374 patents; jury's nonobviousness verdict supported by substantial evidence

The jury could reasonably rely on such evidence to find that Planmeca did not meet its burden to establish by clear and convincing evidence that the asserted claims of the Asserted Patents are invalid for obviousness.
11433: Obviousness of claim 1 of the '037 patent: the court held the Board legally erred by requiring precise quantification of copper reduction for motivation to combine, and that substantial evidence supports only a finding that a POSA would have been motivated to combine Kumada and Debladis '120 to reduce cost, so claim 1 is unpatentable as obvious.

We hold that the Board legally erred in its motivation to combine analysis, and that substantial evidence only supports the conclusion that a person of ordinary skill in the art would have been motivated to combine Kumada and Debladis ’120.
11458: Obviousness: the Board improperly considered the Burrows reference in isolation rather than how a skilled artisan would have combined Burrows with Kovatch or Wise as presented in the petition; the court remanded without deciding obviousness.
We agree, and we conclude that a remand is necessary for the Board to find facts with a proper focus on the combinations as presented in the petition.
11461: Obviousness of claims 1-18 of the '559 patent over Garcia and Randle: the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine the references with a reasonable expectation of success, affirmed on substantial evidence.
Here, substantial evidence supports the Board's determinations that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine Garcia and Randle with a reasonable expectation of success.
11462: Obviousness of the 'accepting' limitation in claims 1 and 10 under the Board's alternative finding, made assuming USAA's claim construction, that the Garcia-Randle combination teaches the accepting limitation; affirmed without resolving the construction dispute.
That finding is supported by substantial evidence.
11495: Obviousness of the independent and composition claims of the '765, '142 and '007 patents over Linhult, Abrahmsén and Hober, including whether a lead-compound analysis was required and whether a skilled artisan would have been motivated to make the G29A modification to Domain C

We affirm the Board’s determination that claims 1–7, 10–20, 23–26 of the ’765 patent, claims 1–3, 5–7, 10–16, 18–20, 23–30 of the ’142 patent, and claims 1–10, 12–14, 16–28, 30–32, and 34–37 of the ’007 patent are unpatentable.
11496: Obviousness of composition claims 4 and 17 of the '765 patent reciting Fab-part binding, an inherent property, without separate reasonable-expectation-of-success analysis
With respect to the composition claims, the claims’ undisputed Fab-binding ability is dispositive.
11497: Obviousness of process claims 4 and 17 of the '142 patent and claims 11 and 29 of the '007 patent reciting Fab-part binding; Board's finding of not unpatentable reversed
we reverse the Board’s determination that the process claims were not shown to have been unpatentable.
11499: Objective indicia (unexpected results) of nonobviousness rejected; natural-result property cannot overcome prima facie obviousness and any Board error was harmless

The same analysis applies to the facts here: Having determined that the independent claims would have been obvious, the recitation of a naturally flowing property of those obvious claims “cannot overcome a prima facie case of obviousness.”
11510: Obviousness of challenged claims of the '740 and '142 patents, including the Board's finding that objective evidence of nonobviousness was entitled to little weight.
we affirm the Board's decision that the challenged claims of the '740 and '142 patents would have been obvious.
11525: Obviousness of claims 1-19 of the '654 patent and claims 1-20 of the '868 patent over Anthony and Hanggie, including whether the combination teaches limitations [1c-2] and [1d-2].
We affirm the Board's determination as to this final disputed aspect of limitation [1d-2].
11538: Obviousness of pending claim 1 over Auger and Yoshida, including the motivation to combine, the weight given to the Dananberg declaration, and hindsight. The Board's obviousness rejection was affirmed.
We conclude that the Board's decision is legally sound and supported by substantial evidence.
11551: Obviousness of claims 2-4, 13, 18 over Amano in view of Gorman and of claims 9, 14, 19 over Amano in view of Flach; the Board's motivation-to-combine findings were supported by substantial evidence and affirmed.
Finally, substantial evidence supported the Board's findings regarding the motivation to combine Amano with Gorman and Flach.
11578: Obviousness of claims 15 and 18 of the '499 patent over KR872; Board found motivation and reasonable expectation of success for lower f-number within claimed range; affirmed.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that a POSA would have been motivated to modify KR872 with an f-number within the claimed range with a reasonable expectation of success.
11582: Obviousness of the design patent: the court overruled the Rosen-Durling test, adopted a new framework, and vacated the Board's nonobviousness determination for reconsideration under that framework without deciding obviousness itself.
we vacate the Board's nonobviousness determination and remand for further proceedings consistent with this opinion.
11597: Obviousness of claim 1 over Dua: Board's finding that Dua teaches the 'prepare data' limitation was supported by substantial evidence, so claims held unpatentable under §103.

11602: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Kato, the Tesla Roadster manual and US 7,671,567; Board found Tesla did not prove the challenged claims 1-10 unpatentable, and the court affirmed.
We agree with the Board that Tesla did not provide sufficient evidence to show that Kato teaches the Charging Control Limitation of the '753 patent.
11643: Obviousness of claim 8 and dependent claims over Nicol and Bhatia; Board held not shown obvious, affirmed
We affirm the Board's determination that Intel failed to prove claim 8 and claims which depend from claim 8 of the '301 patent would have been obvious.
11721: Obviousness of claims 1, 2, 4, 8-10 and 12 over Monroe, Jin and their combination, affirmed as unpatentable.
we affirm the Board's unpatentability determination with respect to claims 1, 2, 4, 8–10, and 12 of the '159 patent.
11727: Obviousness of the D877 design patent; denial of post-verdict motion affirmed because no prior art primary reference was in evidence and motivation to combine was not shown.
We therefore agree with Dynamite that Sherman's failure to place in evidence a prior art primary reference defeats its obviousness challenge under either Rosen/Durling or LKQ
11749: Obviousness of claims of the '839 patent over Lutnick, including the object limitation (single object containing information and instructions) and the user action limitation, with secondary considerations rejected

Rather, the Board agreed with Apple's theory that Lutnick taught a "single," "'self-contained' object . . . including both the program or software [i.e., instructions] and the promotions [i.e., information]."
11791: Obviousness of claim 22, Limitation M (coupling to building electricity), over Imtra 2011 and Imtra 2007; the Board found petitioner failed to show obviousness and the court affirmed.

Thus, the petition and the supporting documentation relied on by the petition are substantial evidence supporting the Board's determination that ELCO failed to show the unpatentability of Limitation M of claim 22.
11828: Obviousness of claims 3 and 4 over Byrne-WO748: motivation to combine (Board found no motivation; affirmed)
We hold that the Board did not err in finding no motivation to combine, so we do not reach the second ground.
11829: Obviousness of claims 2-4 and 15-20 over Raleigh-Byrne: reasonable expectation of success (Board found none; affirmed)

Because Apple has failed to demonstrate error in the Board's interpretation of the petition's Raleigh-Byrne obviousness arguments or in the Board's evaluation of Apple's corresponding evidence for a reasonable expectation of success, we affirm the Board's rejection of the Raleigh-Byrne grounds of unpatentability.
11857: Obviousness of claims 1-3 and 5-7 over Numazaki and Nonaka; court affirmed the Board that these claims are unpatentable as obvious.
We affirm the Board's determination that claims 1–3 and 5–7 are unpatentable
11859: Obviousness of claim 4 (the fixed limitation) over Numazaki; court reversed the Board's finding that claim 4 was not unpatentable, holding the fixed limitation obvious after the Board wrongly ignored Apple's expert testimony.
There is accordingly no reasonable dispute that fixing the two components was desirable because doing so ensured the necessary overlap
11874: Obviousness of all challenged claims of the three patents over the JVM-based prior art combinations; the Board's unpatentability holdings were affirmed.
determining that all challenged claims of U.S. Patent Nos. 9,063,755 ("'755 patent"), 9,471,287 ("'287 patent"), and 9,928,044 ("'044 patent") are unpatentable as obvious. We affirm.
11879: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. § 103 of claims 1-6, 8-12, 14-16, and 18-20 of the '564 patent over Ryu, Hodge, and Stallings, including whether Ryu discloses the 'only after' gaze-detection limitation; Board held the claims unpatentable and the Federal Circuit affirmed.
We conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's conclusion that Ryu, when read as a whole, discloses the "only after" limitation.
11884: Obviousness of the challenged claims over Goldberg and Olden, including motivation to combine, teaching of the request and authorization messages, and teaching of the monitoring function; Board's obviousness conclusion affirmed.
The Board reasonably found that a relevant artisan would have been motivated to combine Olden's "user entitlement and authorization system"
11893: Obviousness of claims 1-20 and 22 of the '570 patent and claims 1-19 and 21 of the '364 patent over the Bird-Ishii combination; Board's unpatentability findings affirmed, including substantial-evidence challenge to the sensor-array-outside-input-area finding.
We affirm the Board's determination that claims 1-20 and 22 of the '570 patent and claims 1-19 and 21 of the '364 patent were shown to be unpatentable
11894: Obviousness of claim 20 of the '364 patent: court held Samsung's petition adequately addressed the 'generating control signals' limitation via claim 13 and that claim 20 is unpatentable, reversing the Board's contrary finding.
Because we affirm the Board's conclusion that claim 13 was shown to be unpatentable, we hold that the Board erred in concluding that claim 20 was not shown to be unpatentable.
11895: Obviousness of claims 30-34, 37-39, 41, 45-49, 57, and 59 over Chickering, Magid and Sclater, including motivation to combine, teaching away, and secondary considerations (nexus).
We therefore affirm the Board’s determination that claims 30–34, 37–39, 41, 45–49, 57, and 59 of the ’884 patent are unpatentable as obvious.
11903: Obviousness of claims of the '028 and '126 patents over Sourcefire reference; Board found all challenged claims obvious and court affirmed
Under that construction, the Board had substantial evidence to find that Sourcefire taught the limitation, and its determination of obviousness is correct on that basis.
11909: Obviousness of claim 15: the court held substantial evidence supported the jury's presumed finding of no motivation to combine, so JMOL of obviousness was properly denied.
We affirm the holding that claim 15 would not have been obvious.
11942: Obviousness of claims 10-14 under the adopted construction; court reversed because obviousness was undisputed once the construction was adopted and Globus made no nonobviousness argument.
as Globus has made no argument that claims 10-14 of the '731 patent are nonobvious under Life Spine's construction, we reverse the judgment of the Board.
11950: Prima facie obviousness of claim 1 over the Hellman/Chou combination, including motivation to combine, was affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
For the foregoing reasons, we agree with what is in effect a prima facie determination of obviousness based on the Hellman/Chou combination.
11951: Nexus of industry praise (AMI press release and agreement) to the challenged claims as objective indicia of nonobviousness; the Board's no-nexus finding was affirmed.
we disagree that the Board erred regarding industry praise
11952: Nexus of the license evidence as objective indicia of nonobviousness; the Board applied an overly strict nexus standard and misread the license, so the finding was vacated and remanded for reconsideration.
we conclude that the Board’s findings regarding the license evidence offered as objective indicia of nonobviousness constitute legal error and were not supported by substantial evidence.
12027: Obviousness of claims 2, 3, 14, and 15 over Liebermann in view of Sears, including substitution of Sears' LEDs into Liebermann's lamps; Board's finding affirmed
the Board correctly determined it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art to substitute Sears' LEDs into Liebermann's lamps 48 to illuminate the claimed work volume
12048: Obviousness of delay-value claims 3, 4, 11, 12, and 20 of the '586 patent over Baker, Bruckert, and McMillin, including whether substantial evidence supports the motivation to combine and whether motivation must be shown claim by claim.
We thus affirm the Board's determination that the delay-value claims would have been obvious over Baker, Bruckert, and McMillin.
12061: Obviousness of claims over Kim based on Figure A, including the alternative theory that Figure A was an obvious variation of Kim's disclosures; Board's findings affirmed.
We thus affirm the Board's findings that Kim discloses Figure A and that Figure A would have been an obvious variation of Kim's disclosures.
12062: Motivation to combine Kim and Koh (wireless earphone limitation); Board's finding affirmed.
We thus conclude substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have combined Kim and Koh.
12063: Whether Kim discloses the switching device limitation; Board's finding affirmed without resolving the claim construction dispute.

12064: Whether Kim discloses the plays a remote device limitation of claim 1 of the '077 and '320 patents; Board's finding affirmed.
We thus affirm the Board's finding that Kim teaches the plays . . . a remote device limitation.
12078: Obviousness of claims 1-7, 9, 10, 20-22, 24 over Hamafuku, Imanaka and Whitman; motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success affirmed as supported by substantial evidence
we note that substantial evidence supports this finding by the Board.
12120: Obviousness of the challenged claims over Jenne and Cohen, including the Board's weighing of secondary considerations (nexus, praise, commercial success, copying); the court affirmed the obviousness holding.
For the reasons above, we conclude that the Board's findings regarding the secondary considerations of non-obviousness are supported by substantial evidence and affirm.
12128: Obviousness over Sorenson in combination with Rao: the Board's finding that Labcorp failed to show a motivation to combine was not legally erroneous and was supported by substantial evidence, so the claims are nonobvious on this ground.
we find that the Board's decision with respect to motivation to combine was not legally erroneous and was supported by substantial evidence.
12148: Obviousness of the asserted claims over Dynatek and Xi; the court found a substantial question of obviousness, which the Federal Circuit affirmed, including rejecting the motivation-to-combine, teaching-away and secondary-considerations arguments.
It is clear from those statements that the district court found a substantial question of obviousness with respect to Dynatek and Xi.
12188: Obviousness of claims 1 and 8-20 over Garcia, Byrne and Singfield; Board found obvious, affirmed (motivation to combine thin client and duplicate detection)
We affirm the Board's decision determining that claims 1 and 8–20 were obvious
12189: Obviousness of dependent claims 2-7 (error processing on mobile phone); Board found not obvious, reversed, claims held obvious
We agree with PNC that the undisputed evidence in the record shows a motivation to combine Garcia and Byrne.
12201: Board's finding that Agin's power control step size teaches the claimed offset is supported by substantial evidence, so claim 9 is obvious on this limitation.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Agin teaches the claimed offset.
12203: Board's finding that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine Agin and Chen is supported by substantial evidence.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's determination that a skilled artisan would have been motivated to combine Agin and Chen.
12205: Board's finding that Chen's weighted average teaching, although used at multiple base stations, would have been applied to a single base station in Agin is supported by substantial evidence.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding.
12208: Obviousness of all claims of the '145 patent over Lebrun in view of Wang, resting on the Board's claim construction.
we agree with the Board's construction of the disputed term and, thus, its conclusion that all claims of the '145 patent are unpatentable based on obviousness.
12210: Obviousness of the asserted claims of the '735 patent over Kondo and other prior art, including motivation to combine, reasonable expectation of success, and secondary considerations; the court affirmed the obviousness holding.
We therefore affirm the district court's obviousness determinations regarding the asserted claims of the '735 patent.
12228: Motivation to combine Watanabe with the Lee Patent for claim 13 was not shown; claim 13 nonobvious over Watanabe combination (Micron appeal)

12230: Obviousness of claim 13 over Lee Application combinations (Intel appeal); nonobvious because limitation 13[b] was not shown
Intel cannot demonstrate that a skilled artisan would have understood its proposed combinations to teach the claim limitation; its obviousness argument must fail.
12231: Obviousness of claim 1 over Park and Kim; no separation of memory cells by dielectric material shown (Intel appeal)

12254: Obviousness of claims 1-11 over Ryan, alone or in combination with other art; affirmed as the Board's unchallenged substantial-evidence finding after the construction was upheld.

12256: Obviousness of independent claims 1 and 10 of the '987 patent over Biderman in view of Gigliotti; Board found the claims obvious and the Federal Circuit affirmed, rejecting DivX's arguments on the scope of the combination and the existence of two stream selection methods in the prior art.

12262: Obviousness of claims 1-3, 9-13 and 16-17 of the '578 patent over Keller '574 or Heusser combined with Yu, including the motivation-to-combine finding and the Henny Penny argument; the court held the claims obvious.
we affirm the Board's holding that the asserted claims would have been obvious and therefore are unpatentable and invalid.

The Board erred by requiring Guardant to show a motivation to combine and a reasonable expectation of success for amplification followed by sequencing, which Travers '075 paragraph 122 discloses in a single embodiment. We determine that the Board erred by requiring Guardant to show that a skilled artisan would have had a motivation to combine the steps of amplification followed by sequencing and would have had a reasonable expectation of success in performing the amplification and sequencing steps because the prior art reference expressly discloses performing those steps in sequence and the Petition did not rely on modifying these two steps to arrive at the claimed invention.
12331: Obviousness of claims of the '833 and '090 patents over Agrawal, Brent, Feitelson, Chen and Compton, including motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success; Board held all challenged claims obvious.

12346: Obviousness of claims 1-4 of the '659 patent over the prior art; no clear error in district court finding that claims were nonobvious; affirmed.

12362: Obviousness of the challenged claims of the '725, '646, '751 and '789 patents over Riddle; Board's finding of unpatentability affirmed on substantial evidence.

12363: Nonobviousness of claim 3 of the '646 patent and claim 34 of the '789 patent over Wakeman; Board's finding that a POSITA would not have been motivated to use an associative cache affirmed on cross-appeal.

12370: Obviousness of the challenged '275 patent claims over Leong and AppleTalkBook; the court held substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the combination does not render the claims obvious, including rejection of the zone theory on the merits.

12386: Obviousness of all challenged claims of the '711, '182, '717 and '293 patents over prior art (Garber, Andersen, Werb)

12421: Obviousness over Littleworth and Middlebrook: the calculating-a-pitch limitation was met by the combination and substantial evidence supported the Board's finding.

the Board correctly construed the petition as arguing that the "calculat[ing] a pitch" limitations were met based on the combination of Littleworth and Middlebrook, and substantial evidence supports the Board's finding.
12422: Obviousness: reason to combine Littleworth and Linder (stereoscopic imaging teachings) was adequately explained and supported by substantial evidence.
we conclude that the Board adequately explained and supported its finding of a reason to combine Littleworth and Linder and find no error in its rejection of Eagle View's rebuttal arguments.
12435: Obviousness over Lumidigm: the asserted claims were not shown to be obvious.
Thus, we affirm the Commission’s conclusion that Apple failed to prove the asserted claims are invalid due to obviousness.
12438: Obviousness under 35 U.S.C. § 103: the Board's holding that claims 1-13 and 16-18 of the '992 patent are unpatentable as obvious was affirmed.

12448: Obviousness of substitute claims: motivation to modify Feldman's request to include current zoom level; Board erred under KSR, so vacated and remanded.

we vacate the Board's finding that there is no motivation to modify Feldman's request to include a 'current zoom level' based on any of Snap's seven prior art references teaching requests relating to zoom levels.
12462: Obviousness under §103 of claims 1, 2, and 6-18 over Castell and Engstrom, including motivation to combine and whether Castell teaches editing of record fields; Board affirmed.
we see no basis for setting aside the Board's decision regarding obviousness.
12495: Obviousness of claims over Armitage and Barone: substantial evidence supports motivation to combine Barone's data-filtering principle with Armitage's system.

12496: Obviousness of claim 25 limitation requiring a software filter executed on firmware: substantial evidence supports finding that Armitage-Barone combination discloses it notwithstanding Barone's analog filtering.

12503: Obviousness of claims 1-8 over Wong and Beauregard, including the receiving, decodes, and deciding/selecting limitations, motivation to combine, and hindsight bias; Board found claims unpatentable and Federal Circuit affirmed.

12587: Obviousness of the 'temporary fixation' claims (claim 38 of the '713 patent and claims 11 and 17 of the '751 patent) over Arnould combined with Zahiri.

12589: Obviousness of dependent claims 34-35 of the '713 patent over Arnould, Zahiri and Myerson '608, including motivation to combine three references.

12590: Obviousness of claim 6 of the '751 patent over Arnould, Zahiri and Myerson '592; the Board's misidentification of Myerson '608 was held harmless.
the Board’s reference to Myerson ’608 is clearly a typographical – and harmless – error.
12608: Obviousness of all challenged claims of the three QuantifiCare patents over Plassmann, affirmed as unpatentable
